> Scroll down for code samples, example requests and responses. Select a language for code samples from the tabs above or the mobile navigation menu.

# Overview

This is the official documentation for the Hetzner Cloud API.

## Introduction

The Hetzner Cloud API operates over HTTPS and uses JSON as its data format. The API is a RESTful API and utilizes HTTP methods and HTTP status codes to specify requests and responses.

As an alternative to working directly with our API you may also consider to use:

- Our CLI program [hcloud](https://github.com/hetznercloud/cli)
- Our [library for Go](https://github.com/hetznercloud/hcloud-go)
- Our [library for Python](https://github.com/hetznercloud/hcloud-python)

You can find even more libraries, tools and integrations on our [Awesome List on GitHub](https://github.com/hetznercloud/awesome-hcloud).

## Getting Started

To get started using the API you first need an API token. Sign in into the [Hetzner Console](https://console.hetzner.com/) choose a Project, go to `Security` → `API Tokens`, and generate a new token. Make sure to copy the token because it won’t be shown to you again. A token is bound to a Project, to interact with the API of another Project you have to create a new token inside the Project. Let’s say your new token is `LRK9DAWQ1ZAEFSrCNEEzLCUwhYX1U3g7wMg4dTlkkDC96fyDuyJ39nVbVjCKSDfj`.

You’re now ready to do your first request against the API. To get a list of all Servers in your Project, issue the example request on the right side using [curl](https://curl.se/).

Make sure to replace the token in the example command with the token you have just created. Since your Project probably does not contain any Servers yet, the example response will look like the response on the right side. We will almost always provide a resource root like `servers` inside the example response. A response can also contain a `meta` object with information like [Pagination](#description/pagination).

**Example Request**

```shell
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer LRK9DAWQ1ZAEFSrCNEEzLCUwhYX1U3g7wMg4dTlkkDC96fyDuyJ39nVbVjCKSDfj" \
  https://api.hetzner.cloud/v1/servers
```

**Example Response**

```json
{
  "servers": [],
  "meta": {
    "pagination": {
      "page": 1,
      "per_page": 25,
      "previous_page": null,
      "next_page": null,
      "last_page": 1,
      "total_entries": 0
    }
  }
}
```

## Authentication

All requests to the Hetzner Cloud API must be authenticated via a API token. Include your secret API token in every request you send to the API with the `Authorization` HTTP header.

To create a new API token for your Project, switch into the [Hetzner Console](https://console.hetzner.com/) choose a Project, go to `Security` → `API Tokens`, and generate a new token.

**Example Authorization header**

```http
Authorization: Bearer LRK9DAWQ1ZAEFSrCNEEzLCUwhYX1U3g7wMg4dTlkkDC96fyDuyJ39nVbVjCKSDfj
```

## Query Parameters

The API makes use of query parameters to sort and filter responses. The parameter names and values must be URI encoded according to [RFC2396](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc2396). Query parameters of type `array` can be used multiple times:

**Example query parameters for pagination**

```
https://api.hetzner.cloud/v1/certificates?page=1&page_size=12
```

**Example use of multiple values for a parameter**

```
https://api.hetzner.cloud/v1/certificates?type=uploaded&type=managed
```

**Example use of an encoded parameter**

```
https://api.hetzner.cloud/v1/certificates?label_selector=key%3Dvalue
```

## Errors

Errors are indicated by HTTP status codes. Further, the response of the request which generated the error contains an error code, an error message, and, optionally, error details. The schema of the error details object depends on the error code.

The error response contains the following keys:

| Keys      | Meaning                                                               |
| --------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `code`    | Short string indicating the type of error (machine-parsable)          |
| `message` | Textual description on what has gone wrong                            |
| `details` | An object providing for details on the error (schema depends on code) |

**Example response**

```json
{
  "error": {
    "code": "invalid_input",
    "message": "invalid input in field 'broken_field': is too long",
    "details": {
      "fields": [
        {
          "name": "broken_field",
          "messages": ["is too long"]
        }
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

### Error Codes

| Status | Code | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `400` | `json_error` | Invalid JSON input in your request. |
| `401` | `unauthorized` | Request was made with an invalid or unknown token. |
| `403` | `forbidden` | Insufficient permissions for this request. |
| `403` | `maintenance` | Cannot perform operation due to maintenance. |
| `403` | `resource_limit_exceeded` | Error when exceeding the maximum quantity of a resource for an account. |
| `404` | `not_found` | Entity not found. |
| `405` | `method_not_allowed` | The request method is not allowed |
| `409` | `uniqueness_error` | One or more of the objects fields must be unique. |
| `409` | `conflict` | The resource has changed during the request, please retry. |
| `410` | `deprecated_api_endpoint` | The API endpoint functionality was removed. |
| `412` | `resource_unavailable` | The requested resource is currently unavailable (e.g. not available for order). |
| `422` | `invalid_input` | Error while parsing or processing the input. |
| `422` | `service_error` | Error within a service. |
| `422` | `unsupported_error` | The corresponding resource does not support the Action. |
| `423` | `locked` | The item you are trying to access is locked (there is already an Action running). |
| `423` | `protected` | The Action you are trying to start is protected for this resource. |
| `429` | `rate_limit_exceeded` | Error when sending too many requests. |
| `500` | `server_error` | Error within the API backend. |
| `502` | `bad_gateway` | The request could not be answered by the API backend, please retry. |
| `503` | `unavailable` | A service or product is currently not available. |
| `504` | `timeout` | The request could not be answered in time, please retry. |

**invalid_input**

```json
{
  "error": {
    "code": "invalid_input",
    "message": "invalid input in field 'broken_field': is too long",
    "details": {
      "fields": [
        {
          "name": "broken_field",
          "messages": ["is too long"]
        }
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

**uniqueness_error**

```json
{
  "error": {
    "code": "uniqueness_error",
    "message": "SSH key with the same fingerprint already exists",
    "details": {
      "fields": [
        {
          "name": "public_key"
        }
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

**resource_limit_exceeded**

```json
{
  "error": {
    "code": "resource_limit_exceeded",
    "message": "project limit exceeded",
    "details": {
      "limits": [
        {
          "name": "project_limit"
        }
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

**deprecated_api_endpoint**

```json
{
  "error": {
    "code": "deprecated_api_endpoint",
    "message": "API functionality was removed",
    "details": {
      "announcement": "https://docs.hetzner.cloud/changelog#2023-07-20-foo-endpoint-is-deprecated"
    }
  }
}
```

## Actions

Actions represent asynchronous tasks within the API, targeting one or more resources. Triggering changes in the API may return a `running` action.

An action should be waited upon, until it reaches either the `success` or `error` state. Avoid polling the action's state too frequently to reduce the risk of exhausting your API requests and hitting the [rate limit](#description/rate-limiting).

If an action fails, it will contain details about the underlying error.

Once the asynchronous tasks have completed and the targeted resources are in a consistent state, the action is marked as succeeded.

In some cases, you may trigger multiple changes at once, and only wait for the returned actions at a later stage.

## Labels

Labels are `key/value` pairs that can be attached to all resources.

Valid label keys have two segments: an optional prefix and name, separated by a slash (`/`). The name segment is required and must be a string of 63 characters or less, beginning and ending with an alphanumeric character (`[a-z0-9A-Z]`) with dashes (`-`), underscores (`_`), dots (`.`), and alphanumerics between. The prefix is optional. If specified, the prefix must be a DNS subdomain: a series of DNS labels separated by dots (`.`), not longer than 253 characters in total, followed by a slash (`/`).

Valid label values must be a string of 63 characters or less and must be empty or begin and end with an alphanumeric character (`[a-z0-9A-Z]`) with dashes (`-`), underscores (`_`), dots (`.`), and alphanumerics between.

The `hetzner.cloud/` prefix is reserved and cannot be used.

**Example Labels**

```json
{
  "labels": {
    "environment": "development",
    "service": "backend",
    "example.com/my": "label",
    "just-a-key": ""
  }
}
```

## Label Selector

For resources with labels, you can filter resources by their labels using the label selector query language.

| Expression           | Meaning                                              |
| -------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------- |
| `k==v` / `k=v`       | Value of key `k` does equal value `v`                |
| `k!=v`               | Value of key `k` does not equal value `v`            |
| `k`                  | Key `k` is present                                   |
| `!k`                 | Key `k` is not present                               |
| `k in (v1,v2,v3)`    | Value of key `k` is `v1`, `v2`, or `v3`              |
| `k notin (v1,v2,v3)` | Value of key `k` is neither `v1`, nor `v2`, nor `v3` |
| `k1==v,!k2`          | Value of key `k1` is `v` and key `k2` is not present |

### Examples

- Returns all resources that have a `env=production` label and that don't have a `type=database` label:

  `env=production,type!=database`

- Returns all resources that have a `env=testing` or `env=staging` label:

  `env in (testing,staging)`

- Returns all resources that don't have a `type` label:

  `!type`

## Pagination

Responses which return multiple items support pagination. If they do support pagination, it can be controlled with following query string parameters:

- A `page` parameter specifies the page to fetch. The number of the first page is 1. For invalid values, page 1 is fetched.
- A `per_page` parameter specifies the number of items returned per page. The default value is 25 and the maximum is 50, unless otherwise specified in the documentation. For invalid values, the default is used.

Responses contain a `Link` header with pagination information. This header is deprecated and will be removed in the future as [announced in the changelog](https://docs.hetzner.cloud/changelog#2026-10-12-link-header-deprecation).

Additionally, if the response body is JSON and the root object is an object, that object has a `pagination` object inside the `meta` object with pagination information:

**Example Pagination**

```json
{
    "servers": [...],
    "meta": {
        "pagination": {
            "page": 2,
            "per_page": 25,
            "previous_page": 1,
            "next_page": 3,
            "last_page": 4,
            "total_entries": 100
        }
    }
}
```

The keys `previous_page`, `next_page`, `last_page`, and `total_entries` may be `null` when on the first page, last page, or when the total number of entries is unknown.

**Example Pagination Link header**

```http
Link: <https://api.hetzner.cloud/v1/actions?page=2&per_page=5>; rel="prev",
      <https://api.hetzner.cloud/v1/actions?page=4&per_page=5>; rel="next",
      <https://api.hetzner.cloud/v1/actions?page=6&per_page=5>; rel="last"
```

Line breaks have been added for display purposes only and responses may only contain some of the above `rel` values.

## Rate Limiting

All requests, whether they are authenticated or not, are subject to rate limiting. If you have reached your limit, your requests will be handled with a `429 Too Many Requests` error. Burst requests are allowed. Responses contain several headers which provide information about your current rate limit status.

- The `RateLimit-Limit` header contains the total number of requests you can perform per hour.
- The `RateLimit-Remaining` header contains the number of requests remaining in the current rate limit time frame.
- The `RateLimit-Reset` header contains a UNIX timestamp of the point in time when your rate limit will have recovered, and you will have the full number of requests available again.

The default limit is 3600 requests per hour and per Project. The number of remaining requests increases gradually. For example, when your limit is 3600 requests per hour, the number of remaining requests will increase by 1 every second.

## Server Metadata

Your Server can discover metadata about itself by doing a HTTP request to specific URLs. The following data is available:

| Data              | Format | Contents                                                     |
| ----------------- | ------ | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
| hostname          | text   | Name of the Server as set in the api                         |
| instance-id       | number | ID of the server                                             |
| public-ipv4       | text   | Primary public IPv4 address                                  |
| private-networks  | yaml   | Details about the private networks the Server is attached to |
| availability-zone | text   | Name of the availability zone that Server runs in            |
| region            | text   | Network zone, e.g. eu-central                                |

**Example: Summary**

```shell
$ curl http://169.254.169.254/hetzner/v1/metadata
```

```yaml
availability-zone: hel1-dc2
hostname: my-server
instance-id: 42
public-ipv4: 1.2.3.4
region: eu-central
```

**Example: Hostname**

```shell
$ curl http://169.254.169.254/hetzner/v1/metadata/hostname
my-server
```

**Example: Instance ID**

```shell
$ curl http://169.254.169.254/hetzner/v1/metadata/instance-id
42
```

**Example: Public IPv4**

```shell
$ curl http://169.254.169.254/hetzner/v1/metadata/public-ipv4
1.2.3.4
```

**Example: Private Networks**

```shell
$ curl http://169.254.169.254/hetzner/v1/metadata/private-networks
```

```yaml
- ip: 10.0.0.2
  alias_ips: [10.0.0.3, 10.0.0.4]
  interface_num: 1
  mac_address: 86:00:00:2a:7d:e0
  network_id: 1234
  network_name: nw-test1
  network: 10.0.0.0/8
  subnet: 10.0.0.0/24
  gateway: 10.0.0.1
- ip: 192.168.0.2
  alias_ips: []
  interface_num: 2
  mac_address: 86:00:00:2a:7d:e1
  network_id: 4321
  network_name: nw-test2
  network: 192.168.0.0/16
  subnet: 192.168.0.0/24
  gateway: 192.168.0.1
```

**Example: Availability Zone**

```shell
$ curl http://169.254.169.254/hetzner/v1/metadata/availability-zone
hel1-dc2
```

**Example: Region**

```shell
$ curl http://169.254.169.254/hetzner/v1/metadata/region
eu-central
```

## Sorting

Some responses which return multiple items support sorting. If they do support sorting the documentation states which fields can be used for sorting. You specify sorting with the `sort` query string parameter. You can sort by multiple fields. You can set the sort direction by appending `:asc` or `:desc` to the field name. By default, ascending sorting is used.

**Example: Sorting**

```
https://api.hetzner.cloud/v1/actions?sort=status
https://api.hetzner.cloud/v1/actions?sort=status:asc
https://api.hetzner.cloud/v1/actions?sort=status:desc
https://api.hetzner.cloud/v1/actions?sort=status:asc&sort=command:desc
```

Sorting parameters are applied in the order they are provided.
Invalid sorting parameters (e.g. providing contrary sorting orders like `sort=status:asc&sort=status:desc`) are ignored.

<h1 id="hetzner-cloud-api-actions">Actions</h1>

Actions represent asynchronous tasks within the API, targeting one or more resources.

See [Actions](#description/actions) for more details.


## Get multiple Actions

<a id="opIdget_actions"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://api.hetzner.cloud/v1/actions?id=42' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /actions`

Returns multiple Action objects specified by the `id` parameter.

**Note**: This endpoint previously allowed listing all actions in the project. This functionality was deprecated in July 2023 and removed on 30 January 2025.

- Announcement: https://docs.hetzner.cloud/changelog#2023-07-20-actions-list-endpoint-is-deprecated
- Removal: https://docs.hetzner.cloud/changelog#2025-01-30-listing-arbitrary-actions-in-the-actions-list-endpoint-is-removed


<h3 id="get-multiple-actions-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|query|[integer(int64)]|true|Filter the actions by ID. May be used multiple times.<br><br>The response will only contain actions matching the specified IDs.<br>|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "actions": [
    {
      "id": 42,
      "command": "start_resource",
      "status": "running",
      "started": "2016-01-30T23:55:00Z",
      "finished": "2016-01-30T23:55:00Z",
      "progress": 100,
      "resources": [
        {
          "id": 42,
          "type": "server"
        }
      ],
      "error": {
        "code": "action_failed",
        "message": "Action failed"
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

> 4xx Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "code": "unauthorized",
    "message": "unable to authenticate",
    "details": null
  }
}
```

> 5xx Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "code": "timeout",
    "message": "request timeout",
    "details": null
  }
}
```

<h3 id="get-multiple-actions-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Request succeeded.|Inline|
|4xx|Client Error|Request failed with a user error.|Inline|
|5xx|Server Error|Request failed with a server error.|Inline|

<h3 id="get-multiple-actions-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|actions|[object]|true|none|none|
|» id|integer(int64)|true|none|ID of the [Action](#description/actions).|
|» command|string|true|none|Command executed in the Action.|
|» status|string|true|none|Status of the Action.|
|» started|string(date-time)|true|none|Point in time when the Action was started (in [RFC3339](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc3339#section-5.6) format).|
|» finished|string \| null(date-time)|true|none|Point in time when the Action was finished (in [RFC3339](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc3339#section-5.6) format). Only set if the Action is finished otherwise null.|
|» progress|integer(int32)|true|none|Progress of the Action in percent.|
|» resources|[object]|true|none|Resources the Action relates to.|
|» » id|integer(int64)|true|none|ID of the Resource.|
|» » type|string|true|none|Type of the Resource.|
|» error|object \| null|true|none|Error message for the Action if an error occurred, otherwise null.|
|» » code|string|true|none|Fixed error code for machines.|
|» » message|string|true|none|Error message for humans.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|» status|running|
|» status|success|
|» status|error|

Status Code **4xx**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|error|object|true|none|none|
|» code|string|true|none|Error code for machines.|
|» message|string|true|none|Error message for humans.|
|» details|object \| null|false|none|Details about the error.|

Status Code **5xx**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|error|object|true|none|none|
|» code|string|true|none|Error code for machines.|
|» message|string|true|none|Error message for humans.|
|» details|object \| null|false|none|Details about the error.|

To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
APIToken

<h1 id="hetzner-cloud-api-certificates">Certificates</h1>

TLS/SSL Certificates prove the identity of a Server and are used to encrypt client traffic.


## List Certificates

<a id="opIdlist_certificates"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.hetzner.cloud/v1/certificates \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /certificates`

Returns all Certificate objects.


<h3 id="list-certificates-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|sort|query|[string]|false|Sort resources by field and direction. May be used multiple times.<br><br>For more information, see "[Sorting](#description/sorting)".<br>|
|name|query|string|false|Filter resources by their name.<br><br>The response will only contain the resources<br>matching exactly the specified name.<br>|
|label_selector|query|string|false|Filter resources by labels.<br><br>The response will only contain resources matching the label selector.<br>For more information, see "[Label Selector](#description/label-selector)".<br>|
|type|query|[string]|false|Filter resources by type. May be used multiple times.<br><br>The response will only contain the resources with the specified type.<br>|
|page|query|integer(int64)|false|Page number to return. For more information, see "[Pagination](#description/pagination)".|
|per_page|query|integer(int64)|false|Maximum number of entries returned per page. For more information, see "[Pagination](#description/pagination)".|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|sort|id|
|sort|id:asc|

## Create a Certificate

<a id="opIdcreate_certificate"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.hetzner.cloud/v1/certificates \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "name": "my website cert",
    "type": "uploaded",
    "certificate": "-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----\n...",
    "private_key": "-----BEGIN PRIVATE KEY-----\n..."
  }'
```

`POST /certificates`

Creates a new Certificate.

The default type **uploaded** allows for uploading your existing `certificate` and `private_key` in PEM format. You have to monitor its expiration date and handle renewal yourself.

In contrast, type **managed** requests a new Certificate from *Let's Encrypt* for the specified `domain_names`. Only domains managed by *Hetzner DNS* are supported. We handle renewal and timely alert the project owner via email if problems occur.

For type `managed` Certificates the `action` key of the response contains the Action that allows for tracking the issuance process. For type `uploaded` Certificates the `action` is always null.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "my website cert",
  "type": "uploaded",
  "certificate": "-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----\n...",
  "private_key": "-----BEGIN PRIVATE KEY-----\n..."
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-certificate-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» name|body|string|true|Name of the Certificate.|
|» labels|body|object|false|User-defined labels (`key/value` pairs) for the Resource.<br>For more information, see "[Labels](#description/labels)".<br>|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|string|false|none|
|» type|body|string|false|Choose between uploading a Certificate in PEM format or requesting a managed *Let's Encrypt* Certificate.|
|» certificate|body|string|false|Certificate and chain in PEM format, in order so that each record directly certifies the one preceding. Required for type `uploaded` Certificates.|
|» private_key|body|string|false|Certificate key in PEM format. Required for type `uploaded` Certificates.|
|» domain_names|body|[string]|false|Domains and subdomains that should be contained in the Certificate issued by *Let's Encrypt*. Required for type `managed` Certificates.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» type|uploaded|
|» type|managed|

> Example responses

> 201 Response

```json
{
  "certificate": {
    "id": 897,
    "name": "my website cert",
    "labels": {
      "key": "value"
    },
    "type": "uploaded",
    "certificate": "-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----\n...",
    "created": "2019-01-08T12:10:00Z",
    "not_valid_before": "2019-01-08T10:00:00Z",
    "not_valid_after": "2019-07-08T09:59:59Z",
    "domain_names": [
      "example.com",
      "webmail.example.com",
      "www.example.com"
    ],
    "fingerprint": "03:c7:55:9b:2a:d1:04:17:09:f6:d0:7f:18:34:63:d4:3e:5f",
    "status": null,
    "used_by": [
      {
        "id": 4711,
        "type": "load_balancer"
      }
    ]
  },
  "action": null
}
```

> 4xx Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "code": "unauthorized",
    "message": "unable to authenticate",
    "details": null
  }
}
```

> 5xx Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "code": "timeout",
    "message": "request timeout",
    "details": null
  }
}
```

## Update a Certificate

<a id="opIdupdate_certificate"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.hetzner.cloud/v1/certificates/42 \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "name": "my website cert",
    "labels": {
      "environment": "prod",
      "example.com/my": "label",
      "just-a-key": ""
    }
  }'
```

`PUT /certificates/{id}`

## Retry Issuance or Renewal

<a id="opIdretry_certificate"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.hetzner.cloud/v1/certificates/42/actions/retry \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`POST /certificates/{id}/actions/retry`

Retry a failed Certificate issuance or renewal.

Only applicable if the type of the Certificate is `managed` and the issuance or renewal status is `failed`.

#### Operation specific errors

| Status | Code | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
|  | `caa_record_does_not_allow_ca` | CAA record does not allow certificate authority |
|  | `ca_dns_validation_failed` | Certificate Authority: DNS validation failed |
|  | `ca_too_many_authorizations_failed_recently` | Certificate Authority: Too many authorizations failed recently |
|  | `ca_too_many_certificates_issued_for_registered_domain` | Certificate Authority: Too many certificates issued for registered domain |
|  | `ca_too_many_duplicate_certificates` | Certificate Authority: Too many duplicate certificates |
|  | `could_not_verify_domain_delegated_to_zone` | Could not verify domain delegated to zone |
|  | `dns_zone_not_found` | DNS zone not found |
|  | `dns_zone_is_secondary_zone` | DNS zone is a secondary zone |

<h1 id="hetzner-cloud-api-data-centers">Data Centers</h1>

Each Datacenter represents a _virtual_ Datacenter which may consist of possibly many physical Datacenters. A physical Datacenter is where [Servers](#tag/servers) are hosted.

See the [Hetzner Locations Docs](https://docs.hetzner.com/cloud/general/locations/#what-datacenters-are-there) for more details about Datacenters.

**Note**: This functionality and endpoints were deprecated in June 2026 and removed on 01 October 2026.

- Announcement: https://docs.hetzner.cloud/changelog#2026-06-02-datacenters-deprecated
- Removal: https://docs.hetzner.cloud/changelog#2026-10-01-datacenters-removed

<h1 id="hetzner-cloud-api-firewalls">Firewalls</h1>

Firewalls can limit the network access to or from your resources.

- When applying a firewall with no `in` rule all inbound traffic will be dropped. The default for `in` is `DROP`.
- When applying a firewall with no `out` rule all outbound traffic will be accepted. The default for `out` is `ACCEPT`.


## List Firewalls

<a id="opIdlist_firewalls"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.hetzner.cloud/v1/firewalls \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /firewalls`

Returns all [Firewalls](#tag/firewalls).

Use the provided URI parameters to modify the result.

|name|query|string|false|Filter resources by their name.<br><br>The response will only contain the resources<br>matching exactly the specified name.<br>|
|label_selector|query|string|false|Filter resources by labels.<br><br>The response will only contain resources matching the label selector.<br>For more information, see "[Label Selector](#description/label-selector)".<br>|
|page|query|integer(int64)|false|Page number to return. For more information, see "[Pagination](#description/pagination)".|

## Create a Firewall

<a id="opIdcreate_firewall"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.hetzner.cloud/v1/firewalls \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "name": "Corporate Intranet Protection",
    "labels": {
      "key": "value"
    },
    "rules": [
      {
        "description": "Allow port 80",
        "direction": "in",
        "source_ips": [
          "192.0.2.2/32",
          "192.0.2.0/24",
          "2001:0db8:9a3b:ee58:5ca:990c:8bc9:c03b/128"
        ],
        "protocol": "tcp",
        "port": "80"
      }
    ],
    "apply_to": [
      {
        "type": "server",
        "server": {
          "id": 42
        }
      }
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /firewalls`

Create a [Firewall](#tag/firewalls).

#### Operation specific errors

| Status | Code | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `422` | `server_already_added` | The [Server](#tag/servers) was applied more than once. |
| `422` | `incompatible_network_type` | The resources network type is not supported by [Firewalls](#tag/firewalls). |
| `422` | `firewall_resource_not_found` | The resource the [Firewall](#tag/firewalls) should be attached to was not found. |


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "Corporate Intranet Protection",
  "labels": {
    "key": "value"
  },
  "rules": [
    {
      "description": "Allow port 80",
      "direction": "in",
      "source_ips": [
        "192.0.2.2/32",
        "192.0.2.0/24",
        "2001:0db8:9a3b:ee58:5ca:990c:8bc9:c03b/128"
      ],
      "protocol": "tcp",
      "port": "80"
    }
  ],
  "apply_to": [
    {
      "type": "server",
      "server": {
        "id": 42
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-firewall-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» name|body|string|true|Name of the [Firewall](#tag/firewalls).<br><br>Must be unique per Project.<br>|
|» labels|body|object|false|User-defined labels (`key/value` pairs) for the Resource.<br>For more information, see "[Labels](#description/labels)".<br>|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|string|false|none|
|» rules|body|[object]|false|Array of rules.<br><br>Rules are limited to 50 entries per [Firewall](#tag/firewalls) and [500 effective rules](https://docs.hetzner.com/cloud/firewalls/overview#limits).<br>|
|» » description|body|string \| null|false|Description of the rule.|
|» » direction|body|string|true|Traffic direction in which the rule should be applied to.<br><br>Use `source_ips` for direction `in` and `destination_ips` for direction `out` to specify IPs.<br>|
|» » source_ips|body|[string]|false|List of permitted IPv4/IPv6 addresses for incoming traffic.<br><br>The `direction` must be set to `in`.<br><br>IPs must be provided in [CIDR block notation](https://wikipedia.org/wiki/CIDR). You can specify 100 CIDR<br>blocks at most.<br><br>The CIDR blocks may refer to networks (with empty host bits) or single hosts.<br>For example, a network could be defined with `10.0.1.0/24` or `2001:db8:ff00:42::/64`,<br>and a single host with `10.0.1.1/32` or `2001:db8:ff00:42::8329/128`.<br><br>Use `0.0.0.0/0` to allow any IPv4 addresses and `::/0` to allow any IPv6 addresses.<br><br>IPv6 CIDRs will be transformed to their canonical form according to [RFC5952](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc5952#section-4).<br>|
|» » destination_ips|body|[string]|false|List of permitted IPv4/IPv6 addresses for outgoing traffic.<br><br>The `direction` must be set to `out`.<br><br>IPs must be in [CIDR block notation](https://wikipedia.org/wiki/CIDR). You can specify 100 CIDR<br>blocks at most.<br><br>The CIDR blocks may refer to networks (with empty host bits) or single hosts.<br>For example, a network could be defined with `10.0.1.0/24` or `2001:db8:ff00:42::/64`,<br>and a single host with `10.0.1.1/32` or `2001:db8:ff00:42::8329/128`.<br><br>Use `0.0.0.0/0` to allow any IPv4 addresses and `::/0` to allow any IPv6 addresses.<br><br>IPv6 CIDRs will be transformed to their canonical form according to [RFC5952](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc5952#section-4).<br>|
|» » protocol|body|string|true|Network protocol to apply the rule for.|
|» » port|body|string|false|Port or port range to apply the rule for.<br><br>Only applicable for protocols `tcp` and `udp`.<br><br>A port range can be specified by separating lower and upper bounds with a dash. `1024-5000` will include<br>all ports starting from 1024 up to port 5000.<br>|
|» apply_to|body|[object]|false|Resources to apply the [Firewall](#tag/firewalls) to.<br><br>Resources added directly are taking precedence over those added via a [Label Selector](#description/label-selector).<br>|
|» » type|body|string|true|Type of the resource.|
|» » server|body|object|false|[Server](#tag/servers) the [Firewall](#tag/firewalls) is applied to.<br><br>Only set for `type` `server`, otherwise `null`.<br>|
|» » » id|body|integer(int64)|true|ID of the [Server](#tag/servers).|
|» » label_selector|body|object|false|[Label Selector](#description/label-selector) the [Firewall](#tag/firewalls) is applied to.<br><br>Only set for `type` `label_selector`, otherwise `null`.<br>|
|» » » selector|body|string|true|The selector.|

## Update a Firewall

<a id="opIdupdate_firewall"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.hetzner.cloud/v1/firewalls/42 \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "name": "new-name",
    "labels": {
      "environment": "prod",
      "example.com/my": "label",
      "just-a-key": ""
    }

```

`PUT /firewalls/{id}`

Update a [Firewall](#tag/firewalls).

In case of a parallel running change on the [Firewall](#tag/firewalls) a `conflict` error will be returned.

    "example.com/my": "label",

## Apply to Resources

<a id="opIdapply_firewall_to_resources"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.hetzner.cloud/v1/firewalls/42/actions/apply_to_resources \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "apply_to": [
      {
        "type": "server",
        "server": {
          "id": 42
        }
      }
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /firewalls/{id}/actions/apply_to_resources`

Applies a [Firewall](#tag/firewalls) to multiple resources.

Supported resources:
- [Servers](#tag/servers) (with a public network interface)
- [Label Selectors](#description/label-selector)

A [Server](#tag/servers) can be applied to [a maximum of 5 Firewalls](https://docs.hetzner.com/cloud/firewalls/overview#limits). This limit
applies to [Servers](#tag/servers) applied via a matching [Label Selector](#description/label-selector) as well.

Updates to resources matching or no longer matching a [Label Selector](#description/label-selector) can take up to a few seconds
to be processed.

A [Firewall](#tag/firewalls) is applied to a resource once the related [Action](#tag/actions) with command `apply_firewall` successfully finished.

#### Operation specific errors

| Status | Code | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `404` | `firewall_resource_not_found` | The resource the [Firewall](#tag/firewalls) should be applied to was not found |
| `422` | `firewall_already_applied` | [Firewall](#tag/firewalls) is already applied to resource |
| `422` | `incompatible_network_type` | The network type of the resource is not supported by [Firewalls](#tag/firewalls) |
| `422` | `private_net_only_server` | The [Server](#tag/servers) the [Firewall](#tag/firewalls) should be applied to has no public interface |


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "apply_to": [
    {
      "type": "server",
      "server": {
        "id": 42
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="apply-to-resources-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|integer(int64)|true|ID of the Firewall.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» apply_to|body|[object]|true|Resources to apply the [Firewall](#tag/firewalls) to.<br><br>Extends existing resources.<br>|
|» » type|body|string|true|Type of the resource.|
|» » server|body|object|false|[Server](#tag/servers) the [Firewall](#tag/firewalls) is applied to.<br><br>Only set for `type` `server`, otherwise `null`.<br>|
|» » » id|body|integer(int64)|true|ID of the [Server](#tag/servers).|
|» » label_selector|body|object|false|[Label Selector](#description/label-selector) the [Firewall](#tag/firewalls) is applied to.<br><br>Only set for `type` `label_selector`, otherwise `null`.<br>|
|» » » selector|body|string|true|The selector.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» » type|server|
|» » type|label_selector|

> Example responses

> 201 Response

```json
{
  "actions": [
    {
      "id": 14,
      "command": "apply_firewall",
      "status": "success",
      "progress": 100,
      "started": "2016-01-30T23:55:00Z",
      "finished": "2016-01-30T23:56:00Z",
      "resources": [
        {
          "id": 42,
          "type": "server"
        },
        {
          "id": 38,
          "type": "firewall"
        }
      ],
      "error": {
        "code": "action_failed",
        "message": "Action failed"
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

  }
}
```

  }
}
```

## Set Rules

<a id="opIdset_firewall_rules"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.hetzner.cloud/v1/firewalls/42/actions/set_rules \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "rules": [
      {
        "description": "Allow port 80",
        "direction": "in",
        "source_ips": [
          "192.0.2.2/32",
          "192.0.2.0/24",
          "2001:0db8:9a3b:ee58:5ca:990c:8bc9:c03b/128"
        ],
        "protocol": "tcp",
        "port": "80"
      }
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /firewalls/{id}/actions/set_rules`

Set the rules of a [Firewall](#tag/firewalls).

Overwrites the existing rules with the given ones. Pass an empty array to remove all rules.

Rules are limited to 50 entries per [Firewall](#tag/firewalls) and [500 effective rules](https://docs.hetzner.com/cloud/firewalls/overview#limits).


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "rules": [
    {
      "description": "Allow port 80",
      "direction": "in",
      "source_ips": [
        "192.0.2.2/32",
        "192.0.2.0/24",
        "2001:0db8:9a3b:ee58:5ca:990c:8bc9:c03b/128"
      ],
      "protocol": "tcp",
      "port": "80"
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="set-rules-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|integer(int64)|true|ID of the Firewall.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» rules|body|[object]|true|Array of rules.<br><br>Rules are limited to 50 entries per [Firewall](#tag/firewalls) and [500 effective rules](https://docs.hetzner.com/cloud/firewalls/overview#limits).<br><br>Existing rules will be replaced.<br>|
|» » description|body|string \| null|false|Description of the rule.|
|» » direction|body|string|true|Traffic direction in which the rule should be applied to.<br><br>Use `source_ips` for direction `in` and `destination_ips` for direction `out` to specify IPs.<br>|
|» » source_ips|body|[string]|false|List of permitted IPv4/IPv6 addresses for incoming traffic.<br><br>The `direction` must be set to `in`.<br><br>IPs must be provided in [CIDR block notation](https://wikipedia.org/wiki/CIDR). You can specify 100 CIDR<br>blocks at most.<br><br>The CIDR blocks may refer to networks (with empty host bits) or single hosts.<br>For example, a network could be defined with `10.0.1.0/24` or `2001:db8:ff00:42::/64`,<br>and a single host with `10.0.1.1/32` or `2001:db8:ff00:42::8329/128`.<br><br>Use `0.0.0.0/0` to allow any IPv4 addresses and `::/0` to allow any IPv6 addresses.<br><br>IPv6 CIDRs will be transformed to their canonical form according to [RFC5952](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc5952#section-4).<br>|
|» » destination_ips|body|[string]|false|List of permitted IPv4/IPv6 addresses for outgoing traffic.<br><br>The `direction` must be set to `out`.<br><br>IPs must be in [CIDR block notation](https://wikipedia.org/wiki/CIDR). You can specify 100 CIDR<br>blocks at most.<br><br>The CIDR blocks may refer to networks (with empty host bits) or single hosts.<br>For example, a network could be defined with `10.0.1.0/24` or `2001:db8:ff00:42::/64`,<br>and a single host with `10.0.1.1/32` or `2001:db8:ff00:42::8329/128`.<br><br>Use `0.0.0.0/0` to allow any IPv4 addresses and `::/0` to allow any IPv6 addresses.<br><br>IPv6 CIDRs will be transformed to their canonical form according to [RFC5952](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc5952#section-4).<br>|
|» » protocol|body|string|true|Network protocol to apply the rule for.|
|» » port|body|string|false|Port or port range to apply the rule for.<br><br>Only applicable for protocols `tcp` and `udp`.<br><br>A port range can be specified by separating lower and upper bounds with a dash. `1024-5000` will include<br>all ports starting from 1024 up to port 5000.<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» » direction|in|
|» » direction|out|
|» » protocol|tcp|
|» » protocol|udp|
|» » protocol|icmp|
|» » protocol|esp|
|» » protocol|gre|

<h1 id="hetzner-cloud-api-floating-ips">Floating IPs</h1>

Floating IPs help you to create highly available setups. You can assign a Floating IP to any Server. The Server can then use this IP. You can reassign it to a different Server at any time, or you can choose to unassign the IP from Servers all together.

Floating IPs can be used globally. This means you can assign a Floating IP to a Server in one Location and later reassign it to a Server in a different Location. For optimal routing and latency Floating IPs should be used in the Location they were created in.

For Floating IPs to work with your Server, you must configure them inside your operation system.

Floating IPs of type `ipv4` use a single IPv4 address as their `ip` property. Floating IPs of type `ipv6` use a /64 network such as `fc00::/64` as their `ip` property. Any IP address within that network can be used on your host.

Floating IPs are billed on a monthly basis.

## Create a Floating IP

<a id="opIdcreate_floating_ip"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.hetzner.cloud/v1/floating_ips \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "type": "ipv6",
    "server": 42,
    "home_location": "fsn1",
    "description": "This describes my resource",
    "name": "my-resource",
    "labels": {
      "environment": "prod",
      "example.com/my": "label",
      "just-a-key": ""
    }
  }'
```

`POST /floating_ips`

Create a [Floating IP](#tag/floating-ips).

Provide the `server` attribute to assign the [Floating IP](#tag/floating-ips) to that server or provide a `home_location` to locate the [Floating IP](#tag/floating-ips) at. Note that the [Floating IP](#tag/floating-ips) can be assigned to a [Server](#tag/servers) in any [Location](#tag/locations) later on. For optimal routing it is advised to use the [Floating IP](#tag/floating-ips) in the same [Location](#tag/locations) it was created in.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "type": "ipv6",
  "server": 42,
  "home_location": "fsn1",
  "description": "This describes my resource",
  "name": "my-resource",
  "labels": {
    "environment": "prod",
    "example.com/my": "label",
    "just-a-key": ""
  }
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-floating-ip-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|true|The `type` argument is required while `home_location` and `server` are mutually exclusive.|
|» type|body|string|true|The Floating IP type.|
|» server|body|integer \| null(int64)|false|[Server](#tag/servers) the [Floating IP](#tag/floating-ips) is assigned to.<br><br>`null` if not assigned.<br>|
|» home_location|body|string \| integer(int64)|false|Home [Location](#tag/locations) for the [Floating IP](#tag/floating-ips).<br><br>Either the ID or the name of the [Location](#tag/locations).<br><br>Only optional if no [Server](#tag/servers) is provided. Routing is optimized for this [Locations](#tag/locations).<br>|
|» » *oneOf*|body|string|false|Home [Location](#tag/locations) for the [Floating IP](#tag/floating-ips).<br><br>Either the ID or the name of the [Location](#tag/locations).<br><br>Only optional if no [Server](#tag/servers) is provided. Routing is optimized for this [Locations](#tag/locations).<br>|
|» » *oneOf*|body|integer(int64)|false|Home [Location](#tag/locations) for the [Floating IP](#tag/floating-ips).<br><br>Either the ID or the name of the [Location](#tag/locations).<br><br>Only optional if no [Server](#tag/servers) is provided. Routing is optimized for this [Locations](#tag/locations).<br>|
|» description|body|string \| null|false|Description of the Resource.|
|» name|body|string|false|Name of the Resource. Must be unique per Project.<br><br>A name will be generated if none is given.<br>|
|» labels|body|object|false|User-defined labels (`key/value` pairs) for the Resource.<br>For more information, see "[Labels](#description/labels)".<br>|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|string|false|none|

## Delete a Floating IP

<a id="opIddelete_floating_ip"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.hetzner.cloud/v1/floating_ips/42 \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`DELETE /floating_ips/{id}`

Deletes a [Floating IP](#tag/floating-ips).

If assigned to a [Server](#tag/servers) the [Floating IP](#tag/floating-ips) will be unassigned automatically until 1 May 2026. After this date, the [Floating IP](#tag/floating-ips) needs to be unassigned before it can be deleted.

#### Operation specific errors

| Status | Code | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `422` | `must_be_unassigned` | Error when IP is still assigned to a Resource. This error will appear as of 1 May 2026. |


<h3 id="delete-a-floating-ip-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|integer(int64)|true|ID of the Floating IP.|

}

## Change reverse DNS records for a Floating IP

<a id="opIdchange_floating_ip_dns_ptr"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.hetzner.cloud/v1/floating_ips/42/actions/change_dns_ptr \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "ip": "2001:db8::1",
    "dns_ptr": "server.example.com"
  }'
```

`POST /floating_ips/{id}/actions/change_dns_ptr`

Change the reverse DNS records for this [Floating IP](#tag/floating-ips).

Allows to modify the PTR records set for the IP address.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "ip": "2001:db8::1",
  "dns_ptr": "server.example.com"
}
```

<h3 id="change-reverse-dns-records-for-a-floating-ip-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|integer(int64)|true|ID of the Floating IP.|
|body|body|object|true|The `ip` attributes specifies for which IP address the record is set. For IPv4 addresses this must be the exact address of the [Floating IP](#tag/floating-ips). For IPv6 addresses this must be a single address within the `/64` subnet of the [Floating IP](#tag/floating-ips).<br><br>The `dns_ptr` attribute specifies the hostname used for the IP address. Must be a fully qualified domain name (FQDN) without trailing dot.<br><br>For IPv6 [Floating IPs](#tag/floating-ips) up to 100 entries can be created.<br>|
|» ip|body|string|true|Single IPv4 or IPv6 address to create pointer for.<br>|
|» dns_ptr|body|string \| null|true|Domain Name to point to.<br><br>PTR record content used for reverse DNS. Set to null to reset (IPv4) to the default value or remove (IPv6) the record.<br>|

<h1 id="hetzner-cloud-api-images">Images</h1>

Images are blueprints for your VM disks. They can be of different types:

### System Images

Distribution Images maintained by us, e.g. “Ubuntu 20.04”

### Snapshot Images

Maintained by you, for example “Ubuntu 20.04 with my own settings”. These are billed per GB per month.

### Backup Images

Daily Backups of your Server. Will automatically be created for Servers which have backups enabled (`POST /servers/{id}/actions/enable_backup`)

Bound to exactly one Server. If you delete the Server, you also delete all backups bound to it. You may convert backup Images to snapshot Images to keep them.

These are billed at 20% of your server price for 7 backup slots.

### App Images

Prebuild images with specific software configurations, e.g. “Wordpress”. All app images are created by us.


## List Images

<a id="opIdlist_images"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.hetzner.cloud/v1/images \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /images`

Returns all Image objects. You can select specific Image types only and sort the results by using URI parameters.


<h3 id="list-images-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|sort|query|[string]|false|Sort resources by field and direction. May be used multiple times.<br><br>For more information, see "[Sorting](#description/sorting)".<br>|
|type|query|[string]|false|Filter resources by type. May be used multiple times.<br><br>The response will only contain the resources with the specified type.<br>|
|status|query|[string]|false|Filter resources by status. May be used multiple times.<br><br>The response will only contain the resources with the specified status.<br>|
|bound_to|query|[string]|false|Filter Images by their linked Server ID. May be used multiple times.<br><br>Only available for Images of type `backup`.<br>|
|include_deprecated|query|boolean|false|Include deprecated Images.|
|name|query|string|false|Filter resources by their name.<br><br>The response will only contain the resources<br>matching exactly the specified name.<br>|
|label_selector|query|string|false|Filter resources by labels.<br><br>The response will only contain resources matching the label selector.<br>For more information, see "[Label Selector](#description/label-selector)".<br>|
|architecture|query|string|false|Filter resources by cpu architecture.<br><br>The response will only contain the resources with the specified cpu architecture.<br>|
|page|query|integer(int64)|false|Page number to return. For more information, see "[Pagination](#description/pagination)".|
|per_page|query|integer(int64)|false|Maximum number of entries returned per page. For more information, see "[Pagination](#description/pagination)".|

## Update an Image

<a id="opIdupdate_image"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.hetzner.cloud/v1/images/42 \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "description": "My new Image description",
    "type": "snapshot",
    "labels": {
      "environment": "prod",
      "example.com/my": "label",
      "just-a-key": ""
    }
  }'
```

`PUT /images/{id}`

Updates the Image. You may change the description, convert a Backup Image to a Snapshot Image or change the Image labels. Only Images of type `snapshot` and `backup` can be updated.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "description": "My new Image description",
  "type": "snapshot",
  "labels": {
    "environment": "prod",
    "example.com/my": "label",
    "just-a-key": ""
  }
}
```

<h3 id="update-an-image-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|integer(int64)|true|ID of the Image.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» description|body|string|false|New description of Image.|
|» type|body|string|false|Destination Image type to convert to.|
|» labels|body|object|false|User-defined labels (`key/value` pairs) for the Resource.<br><br>Note that the set of [Labels](#description/labels) provided in the request will overwrite the<br>existing one.<br><br>For more information, see "[Labels](#description/labels)".<br>|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|string|false|none|

    "id": 4711,

    "status": "available",
    "name": null,
    "description": "My new Image description",
    "image_size": 2.3,

  }
}

<h1 id="hetzner-cloud-api-isos">ISOs</h1>

ISOs are read-only Images of DVDs. While we recommend using our Image functionality to install your Servers we also provide some stock ISOs so you can install more exotic operating systems by yourself.

On request our support uploads a private ISO just for you. These are marked with type `private` and only visible in your Project.

To attach an ISO to your Server use `POST /servers/{id}/actions/attach_iso`.


## List ISOs

<a id="opIdlist_isos"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.hetzner.cloud/v1/isos \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /isos`

Returns all available ISO objects.


<h3 id="list-isos-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
APIToken
</aside>

## Create a Load Balancer

<a id="opIdcreate_load_balancer"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.hetzner.cloud/v1/load_balancers \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "name": "Web Frontend",
    "load_balancer_type": "lb11",
    "algorithm": {
      "type": "round_robin"
    },
    "services": [
      {
        "protocol": "tcp",
        "listen_port": 443,
        "destination_port": 80,
        "proxyprotocol": false,
        "health_check": {
          "protocol": "http",
          "port": 4711,
          "interval": 15,
          "timeout": 10,
          "retries": 3,
          "http": {
            "domain": "example.com",
            "path": "/",
            "response": "{\"status\": \"ok\"}",
            "status_codes": [
              "2??",
              "3??"
            ],
            "tls": false
          }
        }
      }
    ],
    "targets": [
      {
        "type": "server",
        "server": {
          "id": 80,
          "ip": "2001:db8::1"
        },
        "label_selector": {
          "selector": "env=prod"
        },
        "ip": {
          "ip": "203.0.113.1"
        },
        "use_private_ip": true
      }
    ],
    "labels": {
      "environment": "prod",
      "example.com/my": "label",
      "just-a-key": ""
    },
    "public_interface": true,
    "public_net": {
      "ipv4": 42,
      "ipv6": 42
    },
    "network": 123,
    "network_zone": "eu-central",
    "location": "fsn1"
  }'
```

`POST /load_balancers`

Creates a Load Balancer.

#### Operation specific errors

| Status | Code | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `412` | `source_port_already_used` | The source port you are trying to add is already in use |
| `412` | `primary_ip_version_mismatch` | The specified Primary IP has the wrong IP version |
| `422` | `ip_not_owned` | The IP is not owned by the owner of the project of the Load Balancer |
| `422` | `load_balancer_not_attached_to_network` | The Load Balancer is not attached to a network |
| `422` | `resolve_cloud_private_targets_error` | The server you are trying to add as a target is not attached to the same network as the Load Balancer |
| `422` | `resolve_cloud_public_targets_error` | The server that you are trying to add as a public target does not have a public IPv4 address |
| `422` | `target_already_defined` | The Load Balancer target you are trying to define is already defined |
| `422` | `primary_ip_assigned` | The specified Primary IP is already assigned to a resource |
| `422` | `primary_ip_blocked` | The specified Primary IP is blocked |
| `422` | `primary_ip_location_mismatch` | The specified Primary IP is bound to a different Location than the Load Balancer |

## Get a Load Balancer

<a id="opIdget_load_balancer"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.hetzner.cloud/v1/load_balancers/42 \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /load_balancers/{id}`

Gets a specific Load Balancer object.

|id|path|integer(int64)|true|ID of the Load Balancer.|

## Update a Load Balancer

<a id="opIdupdate_load_balancer"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.hetzner.cloud/v1/load_balancers/42 \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "name": "new-name",
    "labels": {
      "environment": "prod",
      "example.com/my": "label",
      "just-a-key": ""
    }
  }'
```

`PUT /load_balancers/{id}`

Updates a Load Balancer. You can update a Load Balancer’s name and a Load Balancer’s labels.

Note: if the Load Balancer object changes during the request, the response will be a “conflict” error.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "new-name",
  "labels": {
    "environment": "prod",
    "example.com/my": "label",
    "just-a-key": ""
  }
}
```

<h3 id="update-a-load-balancer-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|integer(int64)|true|ID of the Load Balancer.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» name|body|string|false|New Load Balancer name.|
|» labels|body|object|false|User-defined labels (`key/value` pairs) for the Resource.<br><br>Note that the set of [Labels](#description/labels) provided in the request will overwrite the<br>existing one.<br><br>For more information, see "[Labels](#description/labels)".<br>|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|string|false|none|

## Get Metrics for a LoadBalancer

<a id="opIdget_load_balancer_metrics"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://api.hetzner.cloud/v1/load_balancers/42/metrics?type=open_connections&start=string&end=string' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /load_balancers/{id}/metrics`

You must specify the type of metric to get: `open_connections`, `connections_per_second`, `requests_per_second` or `bandwidth`. You can also specify more than one type by comma separation, e.g. `requests_per_second,bandwidth`.

Depending on the type you will get different time series data:

|Type | Timeseries | Unit | Description |
|---- |------------|------|-------------|
| open_connections | open_connections | number | Open connections |
| connections_per_second | connections_per_second | connections/s | Connections per second |
| requests_per_second | requests_per_second | requests/s | Requests per second |
| bandwidth | bandwidth.in | bytes/s | Ingress bandwidth |
|| bandwidth.out | bytes/s | Egress bandwidth |

Metrics are available for the last 30 days only.

If you do not provide the step argument we will automatically adjust it so that 200 samples are returned.

We limit the number of samples to a maximum of 500 and will adjust the step parameter accordingly.

|start|query|string|true|Start of period to get Metrics for (must be in [RFC3339](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc3339#section-5.6) format).|
|end|query|string|true|End of period to get Metrics for (must be in [RFC3339](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc3339#section-5.6) format).|
|step|query|string|false|Resolution of results in seconds.|

|type|connections_per_second|
|type|requests_per_second|
|type|bandwidth|

## Add Service

<a id="opIdadd_load_balancer_service"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.hetzner.cloud/v1/load_balancers/42/actions/add_service \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "protocol": "https",
    "listen_port": 443,
    "destination_port": 80,
    "proxyprotocol": false,
    "health_check": {
      "protocol": "http",
      "port": 4711,
      "interval": 15,
      "timeout": 10,
      "retries": 3,
      "http": {
        "domain": "example.com",
        "path": "/",
        "response": "{\"status\": \"ok\"}",
        "status_codes": [
          "2??",
          "3??"
        ],
        "tls": false
      }
    },
    "http": {
      "cookie_name": "HCLBSTICKY",
      "cookie_lifetime": 300,
      "timeout_idle": 50,
      "certificates": [
        897
      ],
      "redirect_http": true,
      "sticky_sessions": true
    }
  }'
```

`POST /load_balancers/{id}/actions/add_service`

Adds a service to a Load Balancer.

#### Operation specific errors

| Status | Code | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `412` | `source_port_already_used` | The source port you are trying to add is already in use |


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "protocol": "https",
  "listen_port": 443,
  "destination_port": 80,
  "proxyprotocol": false,
  "health_check": {
    "protocol": "http",
    "port": 4711,
    "interval": 15,
    "timeout": 10,
    "retries": 3,
    "http": {
      "domain": "example.com",
      "path": "/",
      "response": "{\"status\": \"ok\"}",
      "status_codes": [
        "2??",
        "3??"
      ],
      "tls": false
    }
  },
  "http": {
    "cookie_name": "HCLBSTICKY",
    "cookie_lifetime": 300,
    "timeout_idle": 50,
    "certificates": [
      897
    ],
    "redirect_http": true,
    "sticky_sessions": true
  }
}
```

|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|integer(int64)|true|ID of the Load Balancer.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» protocol|body|string|true|Protocol of the Load Balancer.|
|» listen_port|body|integer|true|Port the Load Balancer listens on.|
|» destination_port|body|integer|true|Port the Load Balancer will balance to.|

|» » interval|body|integer|true|Time interval in seconds health checks are performed.|
|» » timeout|body|integer|true|Time in seconds after an attempt is considered a timeout.|
|» » retries|body|integer|true|Unsuccessful retries needed until a target is considered unhealthy; an unhealthy target needs the same number of successful retries to become healthy again.|
|» » http|body|object|false|Additional configuration for protocol http.|
|» » » domain|body|string \| null|false|Host header to send in the HTTP request. May not contain spaces, percent or backslash symbols. Can be null, in that case no host header is sent.|
|» » » path|body|string|false|HTTP path to use for health checks. May not contain literal spaces, use percent-encoding instead.|
|» » » response|body|string|false|String that must be contained in HTTP response in order to pass the health check.|
|» » » status_codes|body|[string]|false|List of returned HTTP status codes in order to pass the health check. Supports the wildcards `?` for exactly one character and `*` for multiple ones.|
|» » » tls|body|boolean|false|Use HTTPS for health check.|

|» » cookie_lifetime|body|integer|false|Lifetime of the cookie used for sticky sessions (in seconds).|

## Add Target

<a id="opIdadd_load_balancer_target"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.hetzner.cloud/v1/load_balancers/42/actions/add_target \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "type": "server",
    "server": {
      "id": 80,
      "ip": "2001:db8::1"
    },
    "label_selector": {
      "selector": "env=prod"
    },
    "ip": {
      "ip": "203.0.113.1"
    },
    "use_private_ip": true
  }'
```

`POST /load_balancers/{id}/actions/add_target`

Adds a target to a Load Balancer.

#### Operation specific errors

| Status | Code | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `422` | `ip_not_in_vswitch_subnet` | The IP you are trying to add does not belong to the vswitch subnet of the attached network |
| `422` | `ip_not_owned` | The IP you are trying to add as a target is not owned by the Project owner |
| `422` | `ip_not_assigned_to_server` | The specified IP is neither the Primary IPv4 address nor in the IPv6 subnet of the given Server |
| `422` | `load_balancer_public_interface_disabled` | The Load Balancer's public network interface is disabled |
| `422` | `load_balancer_not_attached_to_network` | The Load Balancer is not attached to a network |
| `422` | `network_has_no_vswitch_subnet` | The given IP is private but attached network does not have a vswitch subnet |
| `422` | `resolve_cloud_private_targets_error` | The server you are trying to add as a target is not attached to the same network as the Load Balancer |
| `422` | `resolve_cloud_public_targets_error` | The server that you are trying to add as a public target does not have a public IPv4 address |
| `422` | `target_already_defined` | The Load Balancer target you are trying to define is already defined |


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "type": "server",
  "server": {
    "id": 80,
    "ip": "2001:db8::1"
  },
  "label_selector": {
    "selector": "env=prod"
  },
  "ip": {
    "ip": "203.0.113.1"
  },
  "use_private_ip": true
}
```

<h3 id="add-target-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|integer(int64)|true|ID of the Load Balancer.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» type|body|string|true|Type of the resource.|
|» server|body|object|false|Configuration for type Server, only valid and required if type is `server`.|
|» » id|body|integer(int64)|true|ID of the Server.|
|» » ip|body|string|false|Optional public IP of the Server to use as target.<br>Must be the Primary IPv4 of the Server, or an IPv6 host address within IPv6 /64 subnet of the Server. If omitted, the Primary IPv4 of the Server is used. Must not be a private IP and is only valid for public targets.|
|» label_selector|body|object|false|Configuration for label selector targets, only valid and required if type is `label_selector`.|
|» » selector|body|string|true|Label selector.|
|» ip|body|object|false|Configuration for an IP target. It is only possible to use the (Public or vSwitch) IPs of Hetzner Online Root Servers belonging to the project owner. IPs belonging to other users are blocked. Additionally IPs belonging to services provided by Hetzner Cloud (Servers, Load Balancers, ...) are blocked as well. Only valid and required if type is `ip`.|
|» » ip|body|string|true|IP of a server that belongs to the same customer (public IPv4/IPv6) or private IP in a subnet type vswitch.|
|» use_private_ip|body|boolean|false|Use the private network IP instead of the public IP of the Server, requires the Server and Load Balancer to be in the same network. Only valid for target types `server` and `label_selector`.|

|» type|label_selector|
|» type|ip|

## Change reverse DNS entry for this Load Balancer

<a id="opIdchange_load_balancer_dns_ptr"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.hetzner.cloud/v1/load_balancers/42/actions/change_dns_ptr \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "ip": "2001:db8::1",
    "dns_ptr": "server.example.com"
  }'
```

`POST /load_balancers/{id}/actions/change_dns_ptr`

Changes the hostname that will appear when getting the hostname belonging to the public IPs (IPv4 and IPv6) of this Load Balancer.

Floating IPs assigned to the Server are not affected by this.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "ip": "2001:db8::1",
  "dns_ptr": "server.example.com"
}
```

<h3 id="change-reverse-dns-entry-for-this-load-balancer-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|integer(int64)|true|ID of the Load Balancer.|
|body|body|object|true|Select the IP address for which to change the DNS entry by passing `ip`. It can be either IPv4 or IPv6. The target hostname is set by passing `dns_ptr`, which must be a fully qualified domain name (FQDN) without trailing dot.|
|» ip|body|string|true|Single IPv4 or IPv6 address to create pointer for.<br>|
|» dns_ptr|body|string \| null|true|Domain Name to point to.<br><br>PTR record content used for reverse DNS. Set to null to reset (IPv4) to the default value or remove (IPv6) the record.<br>|

<h1 id="hetzner-cloud-api-load-balancer-types">Load Balancer Types</h1>

Load Balancer types define kinds of Load Balancers offered. Each type has an hourly and a monthly cost. You will pay whichever amount is lower for your usage of this specific Load Balancer. Costs may differ between Locations.

All prices are displayed in the currency of the project owner's account.


## List Load Balancer Types

<a id="opIdlist_load_balancer_types"></a>

<h1 id="hetzner-cloud-api-networks">Networks</h1>

Networks is a private networks feature. These Networks are optional and they coexist with the public network that every Server has by default.

They allow Servers to talk to each other over a dedicated network interface using private IP addresses not available publicly.

The IP addresses are allocated and managed via the API, they must conform to [RFC1918](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc1918#section-3) standard. IPs and network interfaces defined under Networks do not provide public internet connectivity, you will need to use the already existing public network interface for that.

Each network has a user selected `ip_range` which defines all available IP addresses which can be used for Subnets within the Network.

To assign individual IPs to Servers you will need to create Network Subnets, described below.

Currently Networks support IPv4 only.

### Subnets

Subnets divide the `ip_range` from the parent Network object into multiple Subnetworks that you can use for different specific purposes.

For each subnet you need to specify its own `ip_range` which must be contained within the parent Network’s `ip_range`. Additionally each subnet must belong to one of the available Network Zones described below. Subnets can not have overlapping IP ranges.

Currently there are three types of subnet:

- type `cloud` is used to connect cloud Resources into your Network.
- type `server` was used to connect only cloud Servers into your Network. This type is deprecated and is replaced by type cloud.
- type `vswitch` allows you to connect [Dedicated Server vSwitch](https://docs.hetzner.com/robot/dedicated-server/network/vswitch) - and all Dedicated Servers attached to it - into your Network

Subnets of type `vswitch` must set a `vswitch_id` which is the ID of the existing vSwitch in Hetzner Robot that should be coupled.

### Network Zones

Network Zones are groups of Locations which have special high-speed network connections between them. The [Location object](https://docs.hetzner.cloud/reference/cloud#locations-get-a-location) contains the `network_zone` property each Location belongs to. Currently these network zones exist:

| Network Zone | Contains Locations |
| ------------ | ------------------ |
| eu-central   | nbg1, fsn1, hel1   |
| us-east      | ash                |
| us-west      | hil                |
| ap-southeast | sin                |

### IP address management

When a cloud Server is attached to a network without the user specifying an IP it automatically gets an IP address assigned from a subnet of type `server` in the same network zone. If you specify the optional `ip` parameter when attaching then we will try to assign that IP. Keep in mind that the Server’s location must be covered by the Subnet’s Network Zone if you specify an IP, or that at least one Subnet with the zone covering Server’s location must exist.

A cloud Server can also have more than one IP address in a Network by specifying aliases. For details see the [attach to network action](https://docs.hetzner.cloud/reference/cloud#server-actions-attach-a-server-to-a-network).

The following IP addresses are reserved in networks and can not be used:

- the first IP of the network `ip_range` as it will be used as a default gateway for the private Network interface.
- `172.31.1.1` as it is being used as default gateway for our public Network interfaces.

### Coupling Dedicated Servers

By using subnets of type `vswitch` you can couple the Cloud Networks with an existing [Dedicated Server vSwitch](https://docs.hetzner.com/robot/dedicated-server/network/vswitch) and enable dedicated and cloud servers to
talk to each other over the Network.
In order for this to work the dedicated servers may only use IPs from the subnet and must have a special network configuration. Please refer to [FAQ](https://docs.hetzner.com/cloud/networks/connect-dedi-vswitch). vSwitch Layer 2 features are not supported.

### Routes

Networks also support the notion of routes which are automatically applied to private traffic. A route makes sure that all packets for a given `destination` IP prefix will be sent to the address specified in its `gateway`.

## Create a Network

<a id="opIdcreate_network"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.hetzner.cloud/v1/networks \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "name": "mynet",
    "ip_range": "10.0.0.0/16",
    "labels": {
      "environment": "prod",
      "example.com/my": "label",
      "just-a-key": ""
    },
    "subnets": [
      {
        "type": "cloud",
        "ip_range": "10.0.1.0/24",
        "network_zone": "eu-central",
        "vswitch_id": 1000
      }
    ],
    "routes": [
      {
        "destination": "10.100.1.0/24",
        "gateway": "10.0.1.1"
      }
    ],
    "expose_routes_to_vswitch": false
  }'
```

`POST /networks`

Creates a [Network](#tag/networks).

The provided `ip_range` can only be extended later on, but not reduced.

Subnets can be added now or later on using the [add subnet action](#tag/network-actions/add_network_subnet). If you do not specify an `ip_range` for the subnet the first available /24 range will be used.

Routes can be added now or later by using the [add route action](#tag/network-actions/add_network_route).


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "mynet",
  "ip_range": "10.0.0.0/16",
  "labels": {
    "environment": "prod",
    "example.com/my": "label",
    "just-a-key": ""
  },
  "subnets": [
    {
      "type": "cloud",
      "ip_range": "10.0.1.0/24",
      "network_zone": "eu-central",
      "vswitch_id": 1000
    }
  ],
  "routes": [
    {
      "destination": "10.100.1.0/24",
      "gateway": "10.0.1.1"
    }
  ],
  "expose_routes_to_vswitch": false
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-network-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» name|body|string|true|Name of the [Network](#tag/networks).|
|» ip_range|body|string|true|IP range of the [Network](#tag/networks).<br><br>Uses CIDR notation.<br><br>Must span all included subnets. Must be one of the private IPv4 ranges of RFC1918.<br><br>Minimum network size is /24. We highly recommend that you pick a larger [Network](#tag/networks) with a /16 netmask.<br>|
|» labels|body|object|false|User-defined labels (`key/value` pairs) for the Resource.<br>For more information, see "[Labels](#description/labels)".<br>|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|string|false|none|
|» subnets|body|[object]|false|Array of subnets to allocate.|
|» » type|body|string|true|Type of subnet.<br>|
|» » ip_range|body|string|false|IP range of the subnet.<br><br>Uses CIDR notation.<br><br>Must be a subnet of the parent [Networks](#tag/networks) `ip_range`.<br><br>Must not overlap with any other subnets or with any destinations in routes.<br><br>Minimum network size is /30. We highly recommend that you pick a larger subnet with a /24 netmask.<br>|
|» » network_zone|body|string|true|Name of the [Network Zone](#tag/network-zones).<br><br>The [Location](#tag/locations) contains the `network_zone` property it belongs to.<br>|
|» » vswitch_id|body|integer(int64)|false|ID of the robot vSwitch.<br><br>Must only be supplied for subnets of type `vswitch`.<br>|
|» routes|body|[object]|false|Array of routes set in this [Network](#tag/networks).|
|» » destination|body|string|true|Destination network or host of the route.<br><br>Packages addressed for IPs matching the destination IP prefix will be send to the specified gateway.<br><br>Must be one of<br>* private IPv4 ranges of RFC1918<br>* or `0.0.0.0/0`.<br><br>Must not overlap with<br>* an existing ip_range in any subnets<br>* or with any destinations in other routes<br>* or with `172.31.1.1`.<br><br>`172.31.1.1` is being used as a gateway for the public network interface of [Servers](#tag/servers).<br>|
|» » gateway|body|string|true|Gateway of the route.<br><br>Packages addressed for the specified destination will be send to this IP address.<br><br>Cannot be<br>* the first IP of the networks ip_range,<br>* an IP behind a vSwitch or<br>* `172.31.1.1`.<br><br>`172.31.1.1` is being used as a gateway for the public network interface of [Servers](#tag/servers).<br>|
|» expose_routes_to_vswitch|body|boolean|false|Toggle to expose routes to the [Networks](#tag/networks) vSwitch.<br><br>Indicates if the routes from this [Network](#tag/networks) should be exposed to the vSwitch in this [Network](#tag/networks). Only takes effect if a [vSwitch is setup](https://docs.hetzner.com/cloud/networks/connect-dedi-vswitch) in this [Network](#tag/networks).<br>|

|» » type|server|
|» » type|vswitch|

## Update a Network
