## Change IP range of a Network

<a id="opIdchange_network_ip_range"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.hetzner.cloud/v1/networks/42/actions/change_ip_range \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "ip_range": "10.0.0.0/16"
  }'
```

`POST /networks/{id}/actions/change_ip_range`

Changes the IP range of a [Network](#tag/networks).

The following restrictions apply to changing the IP range:
- IP ranges can only be extended and never shrunk.
- IPs can only be added to the end of the existing range, therefore only the netmask is allowed to be changed.

To update the routes on the connected [Servers](#tag/servers), they need to be rebooted or the routes to be updated manually.

For example if the [Network](#tag/networks) has a range of `10.0.0.0/16` to extend it the new range has to start with the IP `10.0.0.0` as well. The netmask `/16` can be changed to a smaller one then `16` therefore increasing the IP range. A valid entry would be `10.0.0.0/15`, `10.0.0.0/14` or `10.0.0.0/13` and so on.

If a change is currently being performed on this [Network](#tag/networks), a error response with code `conflict` will be returned.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "ip_range": "10.0.0.0/16"
}
```

<h3 id="change-ip-range-of-a-network-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|integer(int64)|true|ID of the Network.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» ip_range|body|string|true|IP range of the [Network](#tag/networks).<br><br>Uses CIDR notation.<br><br>Must span all included subnets. Must be one of the private IPv4 ranges of RFC1918.<br><br>Minimum network size is /24. We highly recommend that you pick a larger [Network](#tag/networks) with a /16 netmask.<br>|

> Example responses

> 201 Response

```json
{
  "action": {
    "id": 13,
    "command": "change_ip_range",
    "status": "success",
    "progress": 100,
    "started": "2016-01-30T23:55:00Z",
    "finished": "2016-01-30T23:56:00Z",
    "resources": [
      {
        "id": 4711,
        "type": "network"
      }
    ],
    "error": {
      "code": "action_failed",
      "message": "Action failed"
    }
  }
}
```

> 4xx Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "code": "unauthorized",
    "message": "unable to authenticate",
    "details": null
  }
}
```

> 5xx Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "code": "timeout",
    "message": "request timeout",
    "details": null
  }
}
```

<h1 id="hetzner-cloud-api-placement-groups">Placement Groups</h1>

Placement groups are used to influence the location of interdependent virtual servers in our data centers. The distribution of the different servers within a group is based on a pattern specified in the type. By enforcing certain rules on the placement of servers within our infrastructure, availability can be influenced in a way that fits your needs best.

In `spread` placement groups, all virtual servers will run on different physical servers. This decreases the probability that some servers might fail together.

<h1 id="hetzner-cloud-api-primary-ips">Primary IPs</h1>

Primary IPs help you to create more flexible networking setups. You can assign at most one Primary IP of type `ipv4` and one of type `ipv6` per Server. This Server then uses these IPs.

You can only unassign a Primary IP from a Server when it's powered off. This Primary IP can then be assigned to a different powered off Server, or you can keep it around for later use.

Primary IPs are bound to a specific Location. You can not assign a Primary IP from one Location to a Server in a different Location. If you need this capability use Floating IPs instead.

If your Server's operating system supports cloud-init there is no further configuration needed to make Primary IPs work.

Primary IPs of type `ipv4` use a single IPv4 address as their `ip` property. Primary IPs of type `ipv6` use a /64 network such as `fc00::/64` as their `ip` property. Any IP address within that network can be used on your host.

Primary IPs are billed on an hourly basis.

## Create a Primary IP

<a id="opIdcreate_primary_ip"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.hetzner.cloud/v1/primary_ips \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "name": "my-resource",
    "labels": {
      "environment": "prod",
      "example.com/my": "label",
      "just-a-key": ""
    },
    "type": "ipv6",
    "location": "fsn1",
    "assignee_type": "server",
    "assignee_id": 17,
    "auto_delete": false
  }'
```

`POST /primary_ips`

Create a new [Primary IP](#tag/primary-ips).

Can optionally be assigned to a resource by providing an `assignee_id` and `assignee_type`.

If not assigned to a resource the `location` key needs to be provided. This can be either the ID or the name of the [Location](#tag/locations) this [Primary IP](#tag/primary-ips) shall be created in.

A [Primary IP](#tag/primary-ips) can only be assigned to resource in the same [Location](#tag/locations) later on.

#### Operation specific errors

| Status | Code | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `422` | `server_not_stopped` | The specified [Server](#tag/servers) is running, but needs to be powered off |
| `422` | `server_has_ipv4` | The [Server](#tag/servers) already has an ipv4 address |
| `422` | `server_has_ipv6` | The [Server](#tag/servers) already has an ipv6 address |


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "my-resource",
  "labels": {
    "environment": "prod",
    "example.com/my": "label",
    "just-a-key": ""
  },
  "type": "ipv6",
  "location": "fsn1",
  "assignee_type": "server",
  "assignee_id": 17,
  "auto_delete": false
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-primary-ip-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|true|Request Body for creating a new [Primary IP](#tag/primary-ips).<br><br>The `location` and `assignee_id`/`assignee_type` attributes are mutually exclusive.<br>|
|» name|body|string|true|Name of the Resource. Must be unique per Project.|
|» labels|body|object|false|User-defined labels (`key/value` pairs) for the Resource.<br>For more information, see "[Labels](#description/labels)".<br>|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|string|false|none|
|» type|body|string|true|[Primary IP](#tag/primary-ips) type.|
|» location|body|string \| integer(int64)|false|[Location](#tag/locations) ID or name the [Primary IP](#tag/primary-ips) will be bound to.<br><br>Omit if `assignee_id`/`assignee_type` or `datacenter` are provided.<br>|
|» » *oneOf*|body|string|false|[Location](#tag/locations) ID or name the [Primary IP](#tag/primary-ips) will be bound to.<br><br>Omit if `assignee_id`/`assignee_type` or `datacenter` are provided.<br>|
|» » *oneOf*|body|integer(int64)|false|[Location](#tag/locations) ID or name the [Primary IP](#tag/primary-ips) will be bound to.<br><br>Omit if `assignee_id`/`assignee_type` or `datacenter` are provided.<br>|
|» assignee_type|body|string|false|Type of resource to assign the [Primary IP](#tag/primary-ips) to.<br><br>Omitted if the [Primary IP](#tag/primary-ips) should not get assigned.<br>|
|» assignee_id|body|integer \| null(int64)|false|ID of resource to assign the [Primary IP](#tag/primary-ips) to.<br><br>Omitted if the [Primary IP](#tag/primary-ips) should not get assigned.<br>|
|» auto_delete|body|boolean|false|Auto deletion state.<br><br>If enabled the [Primary IP](#tag/primary-ips) will be deleted once the assigned resource gets deleted.<br>|

`DELETE /primary_ips/{id}`

Deletes a [Primary IP](#tag/primary-ips).

The [Server](#tag/servers) must be powered off (status `off`) in order for this operation to succeed.
If assigned to a [Server](#tag/servers) the [Primary IP](#tag/primary-ips) will be unassigned automatically until 1 May 2026. After this date, the [Primary IP](#tag/primary-ips) needs to be unassigned before it can be deleted.

#### Operation specific errors

| Status | Code | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `422` | `must_be_unassigned` | Error when IP is still assigned to a Resource. This error will appear as of 1 May 2026. |


<h3 id="delete-a-primary-ip-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|integer(int64)|true|ID of the Primary IP.|

## Assign a Primary IP to a resource

<a id="opIdassign_primary_ip"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.hetzner.cloud/v1/primary_ips/42/actions/assign \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "assignee_type": "server",
    "assignee_id": 4711
  }'
```

`POST /primary_ips/{id}/actions/assign`

Assign a [Primary IP](#tag/primary-ips) to a resource.

A [Server](#tag/servers) can only have one [Primary IP](#tag/primary-ips) of type `ipv4` and one of type `ipv6` assigned. If you need more IPs use [Floating IPs](#tag/floating-ips).

A [Server](#tag/servers) must be powered off (status `off`) in order for this operation to succeed.

#### Operation specific errors

| Status | Code | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `422` | `server_not_stopped` | The [Server](#tag/servers) is running, but needs to be powered off |
| `422` | `primary_ip_already_assigned` | [Primary IP](#tag/primary-ips) is already assigned to a different [Server](#tag/servers) |
| `422` | `server_has_ipv4` | The [Server](#tag/servers) already has an IPv4 address |
| `422` | `server_has_ipv6` | The [Server](#tag/servers) already has an IPv6 address |


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "assignee_type": "server",
  "assignee_id": 4711
}
```

<h3 id="assign-a-primary-ip-to-a-resource-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|integer(int64)|true|ID of the Primary IP.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» assignee_type|body|string|true|Type of resource assigning the Primary IP to.|
|» assignee_id|body|integer(int64)|true|ID of a resource of type `assignee_type`.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» assignee_type|server|

> Example responses

> 201 Response

```json
{
  "action": {
    "id": 13,
    "command": "assign_primary_ip",
    "status": "running",
    "progress": 0,
    "started": "2016-01-30T23:50:00Z",
    "finished": null,
    "resources": [
      {
        "id": 42,
        "type": "server"
      },
      {
        "id": 4711,
        "type": "primary_ip"
      }
    ],
    "error": {
      "code": "action_failed",
      "message": "Action failed"
    }
  }
}
```

> 4xx Response

```json
{
```

## Change reverse DNS records for a Primary IP

<a id="opIdchange_primary_ip_dns_ptr"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.hetzner.cloud/v1/primary_ips/42/actions/change_dns_ptr \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "ip": "2001:db8::1",
    "dns_ptr": "server.example.com"
  }'
```

`POST /primary_ips/{id}/actions/change_dns_ptr`

Change the reverse DNS records for this [Primary IP](#tag/primary-ips).

Allows to modify the PTR records set for the IP address.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "ip": "2001:db8::1",
  "dns_ptr": "server.example.com"
}
```

<h3 id="change-reverse-dns-records-for-a-primary-ip-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|integer(int64)|true|ID of the Primary IP.|
|body|body|object|true|The `ip` attributes specifies for which IP address the record is set. For IPv4 addresses this must be the exact address of the [Primary IP](#tag/primary-ips). For IPv6 addresses this must be a single address within the `/64` subnet of the [Primary IP](#tag/primary-ips).<br><br>The `dns_ptr` attribute specifies the hostname used for the IP address. Must be a fully qualified domain name (FQDN) without trailing dot.<br><br>For IPv6 [Primary IPs](#tag/primary-ips) up to 100 entries can be created.<br>|
|» ip|body|string|true|Single IPv4 or IPv6 address to create pointer for.<br>|
|» dns_ptr|body|string \| null|true|Domain Name to point to.<br><br>PTR record content used for reverse DNS. Set to null to reset (IPv4) to the default value or remove (IPv6) the record.<br>|

> Example responses

> 201 Response

```json
{
  "action": {
    "id": 13,
    "command": "change_dns_ptr",
    "status": "success",
    "progress": 100,
    "started": "2016-01-30T23:55:00Z",

      }

    }
  }
}
```

## Unassign a Primary IP from a resource

<a id="opIdunassign_primary_ip"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.hetzner.cloud/v1/primary_ips/42/actions/unassign \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`POST /primary_ips/{id}/actions/unassign`

Unassign a [Primary IP](#tag/primary-ips) from a resource.

A [Server](#tag/servers) must be powered off (status `off`) in order for this operation to succeed.

A [Server](#tag/servers) requires at least one network interface (public or private) to be powered on.

#### Operation specific errors

| Status | Code | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `422` | `server_not_stopped` | The [Server](#tag/servers) is running, but needs to be powered off |
| `422` | `server_is_load_balancer_target` | The [Server](#tag/servers) IPv4 address is a loadbalancer target |


<h3 id="unassign-a-primary-ip-from-a-resource-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|integer(int64)|true|ID of the Primary IP.|

## Create a Server

<a id="opIdcreate_server"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.hetzner.cloud/v1/servers \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "name": "my-server",
    "location": "nbg1",
    "server_type": "cpx22",
    "start_after_create": true,
    "image": "ubuntu-24.04",
    "placement_group": 1,
    "ssh_keys": [
      "my-ssh-key"
    ],
    "volumes": [
      123
    ],
    "networks": [
      456
    ],
    "firewalls": [
      {
        "firewall": 38
      }
    ],
    "user_data": "#cloud-config\nruncmd:\n- [touch, /root/cloud-init-worked]\n",
    "labels": {
      "environment": "prod",
      "example.com/my": "label",
      "just-a-key": ""
    },
    "automount": false,
    "public_net": {
      "enable_ipv4": true,
      "enable_ipv6": true,
      "ipv4": 0,
      "ipv6": 0
    }
  }'
```

`POST /servers`

Creates a new Server. Returns preliminary information about the Server as well as an Action that covers progress of creation.

#### Operation specific errors

| Status | Code | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `412` | `primary_ip_version_mismatch` | The specified Primary IP has the wrong IP Version |
| `422` | `placement_error` | An error during the placement occurred |
| `422` | `primary_ip_assigned` | The specified Primary IP is already assigned to a server |
| `422` | `primary_ip_datacenter_mismatch` | The specified Primary IP is in a different location |


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "my-server",
  "location": "nbg1",
  "server_type": "cpx22",
  "start_after_create": true,
  "image": "ubuntu-24.04",
  "placement_group": 1,
  "ssh_keys": [
    "my-ssh-key"
  ],
  "volumes": [
    123
  ],
  "networks": [
    456
  ],
  "firewalls": [
    {
      "firewall": 38
    }
  ],
  "user_data": "#cloud-config\nruncmd:\n- [touch, /root/cloud-init-worked]\n",
  "labels": {
    "environment": "prod",
    "example.com/my": "label",
    "just-a-key": ""
  },
  "automount": false,
  "public_net": {
    "enable_ipv4": true,
    "enable_ipv6": true,
    "ipv4": 0,
    "ipv6": 0
  }
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-server-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|true|Please note that Server names must be unique per Project and valid hostnames as per RFC 1123 (i.e. may only contain letters, digits, periods, and dashes).<br><br>For `server_type` you can either use the ID as listed in `/server_types` or its name.<br><br>For `image` you can either use the ID as listed in `/images` or its name.<br><br>If you want to create the Server in a Location, you must set `location` to the ID or name as listed in `/locations`.<br><br>Some properties like `start_after_create` or `automount` will trigger Actions after the Server is created. Those Actions are listed in the `next_actions` field in the response.<br><br>For accessing your Server we strongly recommend to use SSH keys by passing the respective key IDs in `ssh_keys`. If you do not specify any `ssh_keys` we will generate a root password for you and return it in the response.<br><br>Please note that provided user-data is stored in our systems. While we take measures to protect it we highly recommend that you don’t use it to store passwords or other sensitive information.<br>|
|» name|body|string|true|Name of the Server to create (must be unique per Project and a valid hostname as per RFC 1123).|
|» location|body|string|false|ID or name of the Location to create the Server in.|
|» server_type|body|string|true|ID or name of the Server type this Server should be created with.|
|» start_after_create|body|boolean|false|This automatically triggers a [Power on a Server-Server Action](#tag/server-actions/poweron_server) after the creation is finished and is returned in the `next_actions` response object.|
|» image|body|string|true|ID or name of the Image the Server is created from.|
|» placement_group|body|integer(int64)|false|ID of the Placement Group the Server should be in.|
|» ssh_keys|body|[string]|false|SSH key IDs (`integer`) or names (`string`) which should be injected into the Server at creation time.|
|» volumes|body|[integer(int64)]|false|Volume IDs which should be attached to the Server at the creation time. Volumes must be in the same Location.|
|» networks|body|[integer(int64)]|false|Network IDs which should be attached to the Server private network interface at the creation time.|
|» firewalls|body|[object]|false|Firewalls which should be applied on the Server's public network interface at creation time.|
|» » firewall|body|integer(int64)|true|ID of the Firewall.|
|» user_data|body|string|false|Cloud-Init user data to use during Server creation. This field is limited to 32KiB.|
|» labels|body|object|false|User-defined labels (`key/value` pairs) for the Resource.<br>For more information, see "[Labels](#description/labels)".<br>|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|string|false|none|
|» automount|body|boolean|false|Auto-mount Volumes after attach.|
|» public_net|body|object|false|Public Network options.|
|» » enable_ipv4|body|boolean|false|Attach an IPv4 on the public NIC. If false, no IPv4 address will be attached.|
|» » enable_ipv6|body|boolean|false|Attach an IPv6 on the public NIC. If false, no IPv6 address will be attached.|
|» » ipv4|body|integer \| null|false|ID of the ipv4 Primary IP to use. If omitted and enable_ipv4 is true, a new ipv4 Primary IP will automatically be created.|
|» » ipv6|body|integer \| null|false|ID of the ipv6 Primary IP to use. If omitted and enable_ipv6 is true, a new ipv6 Primary IP will automatically be created.|

## Get a Server

<a id="opIdget_server"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.hetzner.cloud/v1/servers/42 \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /servers/{id}`

Returns a specific Server object. The Server must exist inside the Project.


<h3 id="get-a-server-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|integer(int64)|true|ID of the Server.|

## Update a Server

<a id="opIdupdate_server"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.hetzner.cloud/v1/servers/42 \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "name": "my-server",
    "labels": {
      "environment": "prod",
      "example.com/my": "label",
      "just-a-key": ""
    }
  }'
```

`PUT /servers/{id}`

Updates a Server. You can update a Server’s name and a Server’s labels.

Please note that Server names must be unique per Project and valid hostnames as per RFC 1123 (i.e. may only contain letters, digits, periods, and dashes).


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "my-server",
  "labels": {
    "environment": "prod",
    "example.com/my": "label",
    "just-a-key": ""
  }
}
```

<h3 id="update-a-server-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|integer(int64)|true|ID of the Server.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» name|body|string|false|New name to set.|
|» labels|body|object|false|User-defined labels (`key/value` pairs) for the Resource.<br><br>Note that the set of [Labels](#description/labels) provided in the request will overwrite the<br>existing one.<br><br>For more information, see "[Labels](#description/labels)".<br>|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|string|false|none|

## Delete a Server

<a id="opIddelete_server"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.hetzner.cloud/v1/servers/42 \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`DELETE /servers/{id}`

Deletes a Server.

This immediately removes the Server from your account, and it is no longer
accessible. Any resources attached to the server (like Volumes, Primary IPs,
Floating IPs, Firewalls, Placement Groups) are detached while the server is deleted.


<h3 id="delete-a-server-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|integer(int64)|true|ID of the Server.|

> Example responses

```json
{
  "action": {
    "id": 42,
    "command": "start_resource",
    "status": "running",
    "started": "2016-01-30T23:55:00Z",
    "finished": "2016-01-30T23:55:00Z",
    "progress": 100,
    "resources": [
      {
        "id": 42,
        "type": "server"
      }
    ],
    "error": {
      "code": "action_failed",
      "message": "Action failed"
    }
  }
}
```

```json
  "error": {
    "code": "unauthorized",
    "message": "unable to authenticate",
    "details": null
  }
}
```

```json
  "error": {
    "code": "timeout",
    "message": "request timeout",
    "details": null
  }
}
```

## Get Metrics for a Server

<a id="opIdget_server_metrics"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://api.hetzner.cloud/v1/servers/42/metrics?type=cpu&start=string&end=string' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /servers/{id}/metrics`

Get Metrics for specified Server.

You must specify the type of metric to get: cpu, disk or network. You can also specify more than one type by comma separation, e.g. cpu,disk.

Depending on the type you will get different time series data

| Type    | Timeseries              | Unit      | Description                                          |
|---------|-------------------------|-----------|------------------------------------------------------|
| cpu     | cpu                     | percent   | Percent CPU usage                                    |
| disk    | disk.0.iops.read        | iop/s     | Number of read IO operations per second              |
|         | disk.0.iops.write       | iop/s     | Number of write IO operations per second             |
|         | disk.0.bandwidth.read   | bytes/s   | Bytes read per second                                |
|         | disk.0.bandwidth.write  | bytes/s   | Bytes written per second                             |
| network | network.0.pps.in        | packets/s | Public Network interface packets per second received |
|         | network.0.pps.out       | packets/s | Public Network interface packets per second sent     |
|         | network.0.bandwidth.in  | bytes/s   | Public Network interface bytes/s received            |
|         | network.0.bandwidth.out | bytes/s   | Public Network interface bytes/s sent                |

Note that the CPU value is not normalized to a fixed 0–100% scale. It is calculated per vCPU: a value of 100 represents full utilization on a 1-vCPU server, and 25% utilization on a 4-vCPU server. To calculate the overall CPU usage, divide the metric value by the number of vCPUs.

Metrics are available for the last 30 days only.

If you do not provide the step argument we will automatically adjust it so that a maximum of 200 samples are returned.

We limit the number of samples returned to a maximum of 500 and will adjust the step parameter accordingly.


<h3 id="get-metrics-for-a-server-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|integer(int64)|true|ID of the Server.|
|type|query|[string]|true|Type of metrics to get.|
|start|query|string|true|Start of period to get Metrics for (must be in [RFC3339](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc3339#section-5.6) format).|
|end|query|string|true|End of period to get Metrics for (must be in [RFC3339](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc3339#section-5.6) format).|
|step|query|string|false|Resolution of results in seconds.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|type|cpu|
|type|disk|
|type|network|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "metrics": {
    "start": "2017-01-01T00:00:00Z",
    "end": "2017-01-01T23:00:00Z",
    "step": 60,
    "time_series": {
      "name_of_timeseries": {
        "values": [
          [
            1435781470.622,
            "42"
          ],
          [
            1435781471.622,
            "43"
          ]
        ]
      }
    }
  }
}
```

> 4xx Response

```json
  "error": {
    "code": "unauthorized",

    "details": null
  }
}
```

```json
  }

```

## Add a Server to a Placement Group

<a id="opIdadd_server_to_placement_group"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.hetzner.cloud/v1/servers/42/actions/add_to_placement_group \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "placement_group": 1
  }'
```

`POST /servers/{id}/actions/add_to_placement_group`

Adds a Server to a Placement Group.

Server must be powered off for this command to succeed.

#### Operation specific errors

| Status | Code | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `422` | `server_not_stopped` | The action requires a stopped server |
| `422` | `already_in_placement_group` | The server is already part of a placement group |


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "placement_group": 1
}
```

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|

|id|path|integer(int64)|true|ID of the Server.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» placement_group|body|integer(int64)|true|ID of Placement Group the Server should be added to.|

## Attach an ISO to a Server

<a id="opIdattach_server_iso"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.hetzner.cloud/v1/servers/42/actions/attach_iso \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "iso": "FreeBSD-11.0-RELEASE-amd64-dvd1"
  }'
```

`POST /servers/{id}/actions/attach_iso`

Attaches an ISO to a Server. The Server will immediately see it as a new disk. An already attached ISO will automatically be detached before the new ISO is attached.

Servers with attached ISOs have a modified boot order: They will try to boot from the ISO first before falling back to hard disk.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "iso": "FreeBSD-11.0-RELEASE-amd64-dvd1"
}
```

<h3 id="attach-an-iso-to-a-server-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|integer(int64)|true|ID of the Server.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» iso|body|string|true|ID or name of ISO to attach to the Server as listed in GET `/isos`.|

> Example responses

> 201 Response

```json
{
  "action": {
    "id": 13,
    "command": "attach_iso",
    "status": "running",
    "progress": 0,
    "started": "2016-01-30T23:50:00Z",
    "finished": null,
    "resources": [

        "id": 42,

}
```

```bash
curl https://api.hetzner.cloud/v1/servers/42/actions/attach_to_network \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \

  -d '{
    "network": 4711,
    "ip": "10.0.1.1",
    "alias_ips": [
      "10.0.1.2"
    ],
    "ip_range": "10.0.1.0/24"
  }'
```

`POST /servers/{id}/actions/attach_to_network`

Attaches a Server to a network. This will complement the fixed public Server interface by adding an additional ethernet interface to the Server which is connected to the specified network.

The Server will get an IP auto assigned from a subnet of type `server` in the same `network_zone`.

Using the `alias_ips` attribute you can also define one or more additional IPs to the Servers. Please note that you will have to configure these IPs by hand on your Server since only the primary IP will be given out by DHCP.

#### Operation specific errors

| Status | Code | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `422` | `server_already_attached` | The server is already attached to the network |
| `422` | `ip_not_available` | The provided Network IP is not available |
| `422` | `no_subnet_available` | No Subnet or IP is available for the Server within the network |
| `422` | `networks_overlap` | The network IP range overlaps with one of the server networks |


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "network": 4711,
  "ip": "10.0.1.1",
  "alias_ips": [
    "10.0.1.2"
  ],
  "ip_range": "10.0.1.0/24"
}
```

<h3 id="attach-a-server-to-a-network-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|integer(int64)|true|ID of the Server.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» network|body|integer(int64)|true|ID of an existing network to attach the Server to.|
|» ip|body|string|false|IP to request to be assigned to this Server; if you do not provide this then you will be auto assigned an IP address.|
|» alias_ips|body|[string]|false|Additional IPs to be assigned to this Server.|
|» ip_range|body|string|false|IP range in CIDR block notation of the subnet to attach to.<br><br>This allows for auto assigning an IP address for a specific subnet.<br>Providing `ip` that is not part of `ip_range` will result in an error.<br>|

> Example responses

```json
    "id": 13,
    "command": "attach_to_network",
    "status": "running",
    "progress": 0,
    "started": "2016-01-30T23:50:00Z",
    "finished": null,
    "resources": [
      {
        "id": 42,
        "type": "server"
      },
      {
        "id": 4711,
        "type": "network"
      }
    ],
    "error": {
      "code": "action_failed",
      "message": "Action failed"
    }
  }
}
```

## Change the Type of a Server

<a id="opIdchange_server_type"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.hetzner.cloud/v1/servers/42/actions/change_type \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "upgrade_disk": true,
    "server_type": "cpx22"
  }'
```

`POST /servers/{id}/actions/change_type`

Changes the type (Cores, RAM and disk sizes) of a Server.

Server must be powered off for this command to succeed.

This copies the content of its disk, and starts it again.

You can only migrate to Server types with the same `storage_type` and equal or bigger disks. Shrinking disks is not possible as it might destroy data.

If the disk gets upgraded, the Server type can not be downgraded any more. If you plan to downgrade the Server type, set `upgrade_disk` to `false`.

#### Operation specific errors

| Status | Code | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `422` | `invalid_server_type` | The server type does not fit for the given server or is deprecated |
| `422` | `server_not_stopped` | The action requires a stopped server |


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "upgrade_disk": true,
  "server_type": "cpx22"
}
```

<h3 id="change-the-type-of-a-server-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|integer(int64)|true|ID of the Server.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» upgrade_disk|body|boolean|true|If false, do not upgrade the disk (this allows downgrading the Server type later).|
|» server_type|body|string|true|ID or name of Server type the Server should migrate to.|

> Example responses

```json
{
  "action": {
    "id": 13,
    "command": "change_server_type",
    "status": "running",
    "progress": 0,
    "started": "2016-01-30T23:50:00Z",
```

## Create Image from a Server

<a id="opIdcreate_server_image"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.hetzner.cloud/v1/servers/42/actions/create_image \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "description": "my image",
    "type": "snapshot",
    "labels": {
      "environment": "prod",
      "example.com/my": "label",
      "just-a-key": ""
    }
  }'
```

`POST /servers/{id}/actions/create_image`

Creates an Image (snapshot) from a Server by copying the contents of its disks. This creates a snapshot of the current state of the disk and copies it into an Image. If the Server is currently running you must make sure that its disk content is consistent. Otherwise, the created Image may not be readable.

To make sure disk content is consistent, we recommend to shut down the Server prior to creating an Image.

You can either create a `backup` Image that is bound to the Server and therefore will be deleted when the Server is deleted, or you can create a `snapshot` Image which is completely independent of the Server it was created from and will survive Server deletion. Backup Images are only available when the backup option is enabled for the Server. Snapshot Images are billed on a per GB basis.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "description": "my image",
  "type": "snapshot",
  "labels": {
    "environment": "prod",
    "example.com/my": "label",
    "just-a-key": ""
  }
}
```

|» labels|body|object|false|User-defined labels (`key/value` pairs) for the Resource.<br>For more information, see "[Labels](#description/labels)".<br>|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|string|false|none|

## Disable Rescue Mode for a Server

<a id="opIddisable_server_rescue"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.hetzner.cloud/v1/servers/42/actions/disable_rescue \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`POST /servers/{id}/actions/disable_rescue`

Disables the Hetzner Rescue System for a Server. This makes a Server start from its disks on next reboot.

Rescue Mode is automatically disabled when you first boot into it or if you do not use it for 60 minutes.

Disabling rescue mode will not reboot your Server — you will have to do this yourself.

## Enable Rescue Mode for a Server

<a id="opIdenable_server_rescue"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.hetzner.cloud/v1/servers/42/actions/enable_rescue \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "type": "linux64",
    "ssh_keys": [
      2323
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /servers/{id}/actions/enable_rescue`

Enable the Hetzner Rescue System for this Server. The next time a Server with enabled rescue mode boots it will start a special minimal Linux distribution designed for repair and reinstall.

In case a Server cannot boot on its own you can use this to access a Server’s disks.

Rescue Mode is automatically disabled when you first boot into it or if you do not use it for 60 minutes.

Enabling rescue mode will not [reboot](https://docs.hetzner.cloud/#server-actions-soft-reboot-a-server) your Server — you will have to do this yourself.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "type": "linux64",
  "ssh_keys": [
    2323
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="enable-rescue-mode-for-a-server-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|integer(int64)|true|ID of the Server.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» type|body|string|false|Type of rescue system to boot.|
|» ssh_keys|body|[integer(int64)]|false|Array of SSH key IDs which should be injected into the rescue system.|

#### Enumerated Values

|» type|linux64|

## Rebuild a Server from an Image

<a id="opIdrebuild_server"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.hetzner.cloud/v1/servers/42/actions/rebuild \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "image": "ubuntu-24.04",
    "user_data": "#cloud-config\nruncmd:\n- [touch, /root/cloud-init-worked]\n"
  }'
```

`POST /servers/{id}/actions/rebuild`

Rebuilds a Server overwriting its disk with the content of an Image, thereby **destroying all data** on the target Server

The Image can either be one you have created earlier (`backup` or `snapshot` Image) or it can be a completely fresh `system` Image provided by us. You can get a list of all available Images with `GET /images`.

Your Server will automatically be powered off before the rebuild command executes.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "image": "ubuntu-24.04",
  "user_data": "#cloud-config\nruncmd:\n- [touch, /root/cloud-init-worked]\n"
}
```

<h3 id="rebuild-a-server-from-an-image-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|integer(int64)|true|ID of the Server.|
|body|body|object|true|To select which Image to rebuild from you can either pass an ID or a name as the `image` argument. Passing a name only works for `system` Images since the other Image types do not have a name set.|
|» image|body|string|true|ID or name of Image to rebuilt from.|
|» user_data|body|string|false|Cloud-Init user data to use during Server rebuild. This field is limited to 32KiB. If not specified, the Server's previous user_data value will be re-used (if any was set).|

> Example responses

> 201 Response

```json
{
  "action": {
    "id": 13,
    "command": "rebuild_server",
    "status": "running",
    "progress": 0,
    "started": "2016-01-30T23:50:00Z",
    "finished": null,
    "resources": [
      {
        "id": 42,
        "type": "server"
      }
    ],
    "error": {

}
```

## Reset a Server

<a id="opIdreset_server"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.hetzner.cloud/v1/servers/42/actions/reset \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`POST /servers/{id}/actions/reset`

Cuts power to a Server and starts it again. This forcefully stops it without giving the Server operating system time to gracefully stop. This may lead to data loss, it’s equivalent to pulling the power cord and plugging it in again. Reset should only be used when reboot does not work.

`POST /servers/{id}/actions/reset_password`

Resets the root password. Only works for Linux systems that are running the qemu guest agent. Server must be powered on (status `running`) in order for this operation to succeed.

## Shutdown a Server

<a id="opIdshutdown_server"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.hetzner.cloud/v1/servers/42/actions/shutdown \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`POST /servers/{id}/actions/shutdown`

Shuts down a Server gracefully by sending an ACPI shutdown request. The Server operating system must support ACPI
and react to the request, otherwise the Server will not shut down. Please note that the `action` status in this case
only reflects whether the action was sent to the server. It does not mean that the server actually shut down
successfully. If you need to ensure that the server is off, use the `poweroff` action.

<h1 id="hetzner-cloud-api-server-types">Server Types</h1>

Server types define kinds of Servers offered. Each type has an hourly and a monthly cost. You will pay whichever cost is lower for your usage of this specific Server. Costs may differ between Locations.

All prices are displayed in the currency of the project owner's account.


## List Server Types

<a id="opIdlist_server_types"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.hetzner.cloud/v1/server_types \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /server_types`

Gets all Server type objects.


<h3 id="list-server-types-parameters">Parameters</h3>

<h1 id="hetzner-cloud-api-ssh-keys">SSH Keys</h1>

SSH keys are public keys you provide to the cloud system. They can be injected into Servers at creation time. We highly recommend that you use keys instead of passwords to manage your Servers.


## List SSH keys

<a id="opIdlist_ssh_keys"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.hetzner.cloud/v1/ssh_keys \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /ssh_keys`

Returns all SSH key objects.

|name|query|string|false|Filter resources by their name.<br><br>The response will only contain the resources<br>matching exactly the specified name.<br>|

## Create an SSH key

<a id="opIdcreate_ssh_key"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.hetzner.cloud/v1/ssh_keys \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "name": "My ssh key",
    "public_key": "ssh-rsa AAAjjk76kgf...Xt",
    "labels": {
      "environment": "prod",
      "example.com/my": "label",
      "just-a-key": ""
    }
  }'
```

`POST /ssh_keys`

Creates a new SSH key with the given `name` and `public_key`. Once an SSH key is created, it can be used in other calls such as creating Servers.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "My ssh key",
  "public_key": "ssh-rsa AAAjjk76kgf...Xt",
  "labels": {
    "environment": "prod",
    "example.com/my": "label",
    "just-a-key": ""
  }
}
```

<h3 id="create-an-ssh-key-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» name|body|string|true|Name of the SSH key.|
|» public_key|body|string|true|Public key.|
|» labels|body|object|false|User-defined labels (`key/value` pairs) for the Resource.<br>For more information, see "[Labels](#description/labels)".<br>|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|string|false|none|

> Example responses

> 201 Response

```json
{
  "ssh_key": {
```

<h1 id="hetzner-cloud-api-volumes">Volumes</h1>

A Volume is a highly-available, scalable, and SSD-based block storage for Servers.

Pricing for Volumes depends on the Volume size and Location, not the actual used storage.

Please see [Hetzner Docs](https://docs.hetzner.com/cloud/#Volumes) for more details about Volumes.


## List Volumes

<a id="opIdlist_volumes"></a>

## Create a Volume

<a id="opIdcreate_volume"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.hetzner.cloud/v1/volumes \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "size": 42,
    "name": "test-database",
    "labels": {
      "key": "value"
    },
    "location": "nbg1",
    "automount": false,
    "format": "xfs"
  }'
```

`POST /volumes`

Creates a new Volume attached to a Server. If you want to create a Volume that is not attached to a Server, you need to provide the `location` key instead of `server`. This can be either the ID or the name of the Location this Volume will be created in. Note that a Volume can be attached to a Server only in the same Location as the Volume itself.

Specifying the Server during Volume creation will automatically attach the Volume to that Server after it has been initialized. In that case, the `next_actions` key in the response is an array which contains a single `attach_volume` action.

The minimum Volume size is 10GB and the maximum size is 10TB (10240GB).

A volume’s name can consist of alphanumeric characters, dashes, underscores, and dots, but has to start and end with an alphanumeric character. The total length is limited to 64 characters. Volume names must be unique per Project.

#### Operation specific errors

| Status | Code | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `422` | `no_space_left_in_location` | There is no volume space left in the given location |


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "size": 42,
  "name": "test-database",
  "labels": {
    "key": "value"
  },
  "location": "nbg1",
  "automount": false,
  "format": "xfs"
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-volume-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» size|body|integer|true|Size of the Volume in GB.|
|» name|body|string|true|Name of the volume.|
|» labels|body|object|false|User-defined labels (`key/value` pairs) for the Resource.<br>For more information, see "[Labels](#description/labels)".<br>|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|string|false|none|
|» automount|body|boolean|false|Auto-mount Volume after attach. `server` must be provided.|
|» format|body|string|false|Format Volume after creation. One of: `xfs`, `ext4`.|
|» location|body|string|false|Location to create the Volume in (can be omitted if Server is specified).|
|» server|body|integer(int64)|false|**Deprecated.** This field is deprecated, use the `assignee` field with `server` as the `type` instead.<br><br>Server to which to attach the Volume once it's created (Volume will be created in the same Location as the server).<br>|
|» assignee|body|object|false|Resource to which to attach the Volume once it's created (Volume will be created in the same Location as the resource).|
|» » id|body|integer(int64)|true|ID of the Resource.|
|» » type|body|string|true|Type of the Resource.|

> 201 Response

```json
    "id": 4711,
    "created": "2016-01-30T23:50:11Z",

      "id": 12,
      "type": "server"
    },

      "id": 1,
      "name": "fsn1",

      "country": "DE",

      "latitude": 50.47612,
      "longitude": 12.370071,
      "network_zone": "eu-central"
    },

    },

    },

  },

    "status": "running",
```

<h1 id="hetzner-cloud-api-zones">Zones</h1>

A Zone represents a [Domain Name System (DNS) zone](https://wikipedia.org/wiki/DNS_zone) managed by Hetzner authoritative nameservers.
Please see [Hetzner Docs](https://docs.hetzner.com/dns-console/dns/general/dns-overview#the-difference-between-domain-and-zone) for the difference between zones and domains.

This API supports all zone names with [well-known public suffixes](https://publicsuffix.org/) (e.g. `.de`, `.com`, `.co.uk`).
Subdomains are not supported.

<h3 id="tag/zones/zone-modes">Zone Modes</h3>

This API supports two types of zone modes.

- In _primary_ mode, resource record sets ([RRSets](#tag/zone-rrsets)) and resource records (RRs) are managed via the Cloud API or Hetzner Console.
- In _secondary_ mode, Hetzner's nameservers query [RRSets](#tag/zone-rrsets) and RRs from given primary nameservers via [AXFR](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DNS_zone_transfer).

The zone mode cannot be changed, the zone must be deleted and re-created with a new mode.

### SOA Serial

For zones in primary mode, Hetzner automatically increases the `SOA` record serial number.
As convention, a `YYYYMMDDnn` format with incrementing `nn` is used.

<h3 id="tag/zones/zone-file-import">Zone file import</h3>

This API supports importing a zone file in BIND (RFC [1034](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc1034)/[1035](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc1035)) format.

Importing a zone file is only applicable for [Zones](#tag/zones) in primary mode.

During an import:

- An `$ORIGIN` directive may be present, it must match the [Zone](#tag/zones)'s name with an ending dot
- A `$TTL` directive may be present, it is used as new default [Zone](#tag/zones) Time To Live (TTL)
- Only `IN` (internet) class records are allowed
- The assigned authoritative Hetzner nameservers must be present as `NS` records
- A `SOA` record must be present
- Comments are discarded

Zone file example:

```dns
$ORIGIN	example.com.
$TTL	3600

@	IN	SOA	hydrogen.ns.hetzner.com. dns.hetzner.com. 2024010100 86400 10800 3600000 3600

@	IN	10800	NS	hydrogen.ns.hetzner.com. ; Some comment.
@	IN	10800	NS	oxygen.ns.hetzner.com.
@	IN	10800	NS	helium.ns.hetzner.de.
```

## Create a Zone

<a id="opIdcreate_zone"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.hetzner.cloud/v1/zones \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "name": "example.com",
    "mode": "primary",
    "ttl": 10800,
    "labels": {
      "key": "value"
    },
    "rrsets": [
      {
        "name": "www",
        "type": "A",
        "records": [
          {
            "value": "198.51.100.1",
            "comment": "My web server at Hetzner Cloud."
          }
        ]
      }
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /zones`

Creates a [Zone](#tag/zones).

A default `SOA` and three `NS` resource records with the assigned Hetzner
nameservers are created automatically.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "example.com",
  "mode": "primary",
  "ttl": 10800,
  "labels": {
    "key": "value"
  },
  "rrsets": [
    {
      "name": "www",
      "type": "A",
      "records": [
        {
          "value": "198.51.100.1",
          "comment": "My web server at Hetzner Cloud."
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-zone-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» name|body|string|true|Name of the [Zone](#tag/zones).<br><br>All names with [well-known public suffixes](https://publicsuffix.org/) (e.g. `.de`,<br>`.com`, `.co.uk`) are supported. Subdomains are not supported.<br><br>The name must be in lower case and must not end with a dot.<br>[Internationalized domain<br>names](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Internationalized_domain_name) must be<br>transcribed to [Punycode](https://wikipedia.org/wiki/Punycode) representation with<br>ACE prefix, e.g. `xn--mnchen-3ya.de` (`münchen.de`).<br>|

## Get a Zone

<a id="opIdget_zone"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.hetzner.cloud/v1/zones/string \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /zones/{id_or_name}`

Returns a single [Zone](#tag/zones).


<h3 id="get-a-zone-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id_or_name|path|string|true|ID or Name of the Zone.|

## Update a Zone

<a id="opIdupdate_zone"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.hetzner.cloud/v1/zones/string \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "labels": {
      "environment": "prod",
      "example.com/my": "label",
      "just-a-key": ""
    }
  }'
```

`PUT /zones/{id_or_name}`

Updates a [Zone](#tag/zones).

To modify resource record sets ([RRSets](#tag/zone-rrsets)), use the [RRSet Actions
endpoints](#tag/zone-rrset-actions).


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "labels": {
    "environment": "prod",
    "example.com/my": "label",
    "just-a-key": ""
  }
}
```

<h3 id="update-a-zone-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id_or_name|path|string|true|ID or Name of the Zone.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» labels|body|object|false|User-defined labels (`key/value` pairs) for the Resource.<br><br>Note that the set of [Labels](#description/labels) provided in the request will overwrite the<br>existing one.<br><br>For more information, see "[Labels](#description/labels)".<br>|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|string|false|none|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "zone": {
    "id": 42,
    "name": "example.com",
    "mode": "primary",
    "status": "ok",
    "ttl": 3600,
    "record_count": 4,
    "protection": {
      "delete": false
    },
    "labels": {
      "key": "value"
    },
    "created": "2016-01-30T23:50:00Z",
    "registrar": "hetzner",
    "authoritative_nameservers": {
      "assigned": [
        "hydrogen.ns.hetzner.com.",
        "oxygen.ns.hetzner.com.",
        "helium.ns.hetzner.de."
      ],
      "delegated": [
        "hydrogen.ns.hetzner.com.",
        "oxygen.ns.hetzner.com.",
        "helium.ns.hetzner.de."
      ],
      "delegation_last_check": "2016-01-30T23:50:00Z",
      "delegation_status": "valid"
    }
  }
}
```

```json
  "error": {
    "code": "unauthorized",

    "details": null
  }
}
```

```json
  "error": {
```

## Export a Zone file

<a id="opIdget_zone_zonefile"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.hetzner.cloud/v1/zones/string/zonefile \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /zones/{id_or_name}/zonefile`

Returns a generated [Zone](#tag/zones) file in BIND (RFC [1034](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc1034)/[1035](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc1035)) format.

Only applicable for [Zones](#tag/zones) in primary mode.

#### Operation specific errors

| Status | Code | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `422` | `incorrect_zone_mode` | This operation is not supported for this Zone's `mode`. |


<h3 id="export-a-zone-file-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id_or_name|path|string|true|ID or Name of the Zone.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "zonefile": "$ORIGIN\texample.com.\n$TTL\t3600\n\n@\tIN\tSOA\thydrogen.ns.hetzner.com. dns.hetzner.com. 2024010100 86400 10800 3600000 3600\n\n@\tIN\t10800\tNS\thydrogen.ns.hetzner.com. ; Some comment.\n@\tIN\t10800\tNS\toxygen.ns.hetzner.com.\n@\tIN\t10800\tNS\thelium.ns.hetzner.de.\n"
}
```

> 4xx Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "code": "unauthorized",
    "message": "unable to authenticate",
    "details": null
  }
}
```

> 5xx Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "code": "timeout",
    "message": "request timeout",
    "details": null
  }
}
```

## Change a Zone's Primary Nameservers

<a id="opIdchange_zone_primary_nameservers"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.hetzner.cloud/v1/zones/string/actions/change_primary_nameservers \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "primary_nameservers": [
      {
        "address": "198.51.100.1",
        "port": 53
      },
      {
        "address": "203.0.113.1",
        "port": 53
      }
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /zones/{id_or_name}/actions/change_primary_nameservers`

Overwrites the primary nameservers of a [Zone](#tag/zones).

Only applicable for [Zones](#tag/zones) in secondary mode.

#### Operation specific errors

| Status | Code | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `422` | `incorrect_zone_mode` | This operation is not supported for this Zone's `mode`. |


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "primary_nameservers": [
    {
      "address": "198.51.100.1",
      "port": 53
    },
    {
      "address": "203.0.113.1",
      "port": 53
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="change-a-zones-primary-nameservers-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id_or_name|path|string|true|ID or Name of the Zone.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» primary_nameservers|body|[object]|true|Primary nameservers of the [Zone](#tag/zones).|
|» » address|body|string|true|Public IPv4 or IPv6 address of the primary nameserver.<br><br>Must be unique across all primary nameservers of this zone.<br>|
|» » port|body|integer|false|Port of the primary nameserver.|
|» » tsig_key|body|string|false|[Transaction signature (TSIG)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/TSIG) key to use<br>for the zone transfer. Must be base64 encoded.<br>|
|» » tsig_algorithm|body|string|false|[Transaction signature (TSIG)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/TSIG) algorithm<br>used to generate the TSIG key.<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» » tsig_algorithm|hmac-md5|
|» » tsig_algorithm|hmac-sha1|
|» » tsig_algorithm|hmac-sha256|

> Example responses

```json
  "action": {
    "id": 1,
    "command": "change_primary_nameservers",
    "status": "running",
    "progress": 50,
    "started": "2016-01-30T23:55:00Z",
    "finished": null,
    "resources": [
      {
        "id": 42,
        "type": "zone"
      }
    ],
    "error": null
  }
}
```

> 4xx Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "code": "unauthorized",

    "details": null
  }
}
```

```json
{
  "error": {
    "code": "timeout",

  }
}
```

## Change a Zone's Default TTL

<a id="opIdchange_zone_ttl"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.hetzner.cloud/v1/zones/string/actions/change_ttl \

  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \

  }'
```

`POST /zones/{id_or_name}/actions/change_ttl`

Changes the default Time To Live (TTL) of a [Zone](#tag/zones).

This TTL is used for [RRSets](#tag/zone-rrsets) that do not explicitly define a TTL.

Only applicable for [Zones](#tag/zones) in primary mode.

|» ttl|body|integer|true|Default Time To Live (TTL) of the [Zone](#tag/zones).<br><br>Must be in between 60s and 2147483647s.<br><br>This TTL is used for [RRSets](#tag/zone-rrsets) that do not explicitly define a TTL.<br>|

## Import a Zone file

<a id="opIdimport_zone_zonefile"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.hetzner.cloud/v1/zones/string/actions/import_zonefile \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "zonefile": "$ORIGIN\texample.com.\n$TTL\t3600\n\n@\tIN\tSOA\thydrogen.ns.hetzner.com. dns.hetzner.com. 2024010100 86400 10800 3600000 3600\n\n@\tIN\t10800\tNS\thydrogen.ns.hetzner.com. ; Some comment.\n@\tIN\t10800\tNS\toxygen.ns.hetzner.com.\n@\tIN\t10800\tNS\thelium.ns.hetzner.de.\n"
  }'
```

`POST /zones/{id_or_name}/actions/import_zonefile`

Imports a zone file, replacing all resource record sets ([RRSets](#tag/zone-rrsets)).

The import will fail if existing [RRSet](#tag/zone-rrsets) are `change` protected.

See [Zone file import](#tag/zones/zone-file-import) for more details.
Only applicable for [Zones](#tag/zones) in primary mode.

#### Operation specific errors

| Status | Code | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `422` | `incorrect_zone_mode` | This operation is not supported for this Zone's `mode`. |

```json
}
```

<h1 id="hetzner-cloud-api-zone-rrsets">Zone RRSets</h1>

This API operates on resource record sets (RRSets) instead of individual resource records (RRs).
An RRSet is identified by a name and type. For example, the two RRs

- (name: `@`, type: `MX`, value: `10 smtp.example.com.`) and
- (name: `@`, type: `MX`, value: `20 smtp-backup.example.com.`)

are part of the RRSet identified by (name: `@`, type: `MX`).

Please see [Hetzner Docs](https://docs.hetzner.com/networking/dns/record-types/overview) for more information on types.


## List RRSets

<a id="opIdlist_zone_rrsets"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.hetzner.cloud/v1/zones/string/rrsets \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /zones/{id_or_name}/rrsets`

Returns all [RRSets](#tag/zone-rrsets) in the [Zone](#tag/zones).

Use the provided URI parameters to modify the result.

Only applicable for [Zones](#tag/zones) in primary mode.

#### Operation specific errors

| Status | Code | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `422` | `incorrect_zone_mode` | This operation is not supported for this Zone's `mode`. |

|type|query|[string]|false|Filter resources by their type. May be used multiple times.<br><br>The response will only contain resources matching the specified types.<br>|
|label_selector|query|string|false|Filter resources by labels.<br><br>The response will only contain resources matching the label selector.<br>For more information, see "[Label Selector](#description/label-selector)".<br>|
|sort|query|[string]|false|Sort resources by field and direction. May be used multiple times.<br><br>For more information, see "[Sorting](#description/sorting)".<br>|
|page|query|integer(int64)|false|Page number to return. For more information, see "[Pagination](#description/pagination)".|
|per_page|query|integer(int64)|false|Maximum number of entries returned per page. For more information, see "[Pagination](#description/pagination)".|

#### Enumerated Values

|type|TLSA|
|type|TXT|

|sort|id:desc|

|sort|name:desc|

|sort|created:asc|

<a id="opIdadd_zone_rrset_records"></a>

```bash
curl https://api.hetzner.cloud/v1/zones/string/rrsets/www/A/actions/add_records \

      }
    ]
```

`POST /zones/{id_or_name}/rrsets/{rr_name}/{rr_type}/actions/add_records`

Adds resource records (RRs) to an [RRSet](#tag/zone-rrsets) in the [Zone](#tag/zones).

For convenience, the [RRSet](#tag/zone-rrsets) will be automatically created if it doesn't exist. Otherwise, the new
records are appended to the existing [RRSet](#tag/zone-rrsets).

Only applicable for [Zones](#tag/zones) in primary mode.

#### Operation specific errors

| Status | Code | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |

## Update Records of an RRSet

<a id="opIdupdate_zone_rrset_records"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.hetzner.cloud/v1/zones/string/rrsets/www/A/actions/update_records \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "records": [
      {
        "value": "198.51.100.1",
        "comment": "My web server at Hetzner Cloud."
      }
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /zones/{id_or_name}/rrsets/{rr_name}/{rr_type}/actions/update_records`

Updates resource records' (RRs) comments of an existing [RRSet](#tag/zone-rrsets) in the [Zone](#tag/zones).

Only applicable for [Zones](#tag/zones) in primary mode.

#### Operation specific errors

| Status | Code | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `422` | `incorrect_zone_mode` | This operation is not supported for this Zone's `mode`. |


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "records": [
    {
      "value": "198.51.100.1",
      "comment": "My web server at Hetzner Cloud."
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="update-records-of-an-rrset-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id_or_name|path|string|true|ID or Name of the Zone.|
|rr_name|path|string|true|none|
|rr_type|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» records|body|[object]|true|Records to update in the [RRSet](#tag/zone-rrsets).<br><br>Must not be empty and must only contain distinct record values.<br>|
|» » value|body|string|true|Value of the record to update.<br>|
|» » comment|body|string|true|New comment for the record.<br>|
